entries.name: AutosavePolicy
entries.doc:
When the loaded slot writes itself: on each listed trigger, with `intervalSeconds` for the `interval`
timer.

entries.name: AutosaveTrigger
entries.doc: What can make the loaded slot write itself (M5 spec §4.4).
entries.signature: type AutosaveTrigger = 'screen-exit' | 'round-end' | 'background' | 'interval'

entries.name: Camera2d
entries.doc:
A presentation-only 2D camera over one container: it follows a target, shakes, and writes only that
container's transform, never a sim value.

entries.name: Camera2dOptions
entries.doc: How `createCamera2d` frames the world: the view's size, and optionally a follow, bounds and zoom.

entries.name: CameraRect
entries.doc: A world-space rectangle, in logical px: `Camera2dOptions.bounds`.

entries.name: Command
entries.doc: Input to the sim (spec §4.4 rule 4). `source` is a player slot (u8), `seq` a per-source counter (u32).
entries.signature:
interface Command {
  readonly tick: number
  readonly source: number
  readonly seq: number
  readonly type: string
  readonly payload: unknown
}

entries.name: CommandDef
entries.doc:
A command the sim accepts as input: an id and the Zod schema its payload must match. Create one with
`defineCommand`.

entries.name: ComponentDef
entries.doc:
A component: a stable id and a flat record of typed fields. Create one with `defineComponent`; game code
addresses entity data through the definition, never through `trait`.

entries.name: createCamera2d
entries.doc:
A camera writing `stage`'s transform (usually `PixiStage.world`). `seed` fixes the shake's random sequence,
so a shake looks the same in every run and visual test.

entries.name: defaultContent
entries.doc: The default flow `title → play ⇄ paused → title`, with `paused ⇄ settings` (M4.4), and its hash.

entries.name: defaultScreens
entries.doc:
The title, play, paused and settings screens (DX spec §7, M4.4) over the default content's flow
(`title → play ⇄ paused → title`, `paused ⇄ settings`).

The screens share one sim: play creates it on first entry (seed, plugins, content, then `setup`),
paused keeps it, and the title drops it, so Quit to title and Play start again at tick 0. A runtime that shuts
down with the sim alive drops it too, whichever screen is current (DX.2c). Returning
from paused re-sends the whole state to the renderer (G-5): `AppLoop.run` resets the renderer, so
play restores the sim's own snapshot, which makes the next step a resync.

entries.name: defineCommand
entries.doc:
Defines a command by id and payload schema. Throws for an id that is not lower-case words separated by dots
or dashes.

entries.name: defineComponent
entries.doc:
Defines a component from an id (lower-case words separated by dots or dashes) and its fields by name and
type. `render: false` keeps it out of the renderer's deltas. Throws for a bad id, no fields, a bad field
name or an unknown field type.

entries.name: DefinedGame
entries.doc: The runtime's `GameDefinition`, plus what the screens and the golden replay read from the spec.

entries.name: defineEvent
entries.doc:
Defines an event by id and payload schema, to emit from a system with `ctx.emit`. Events come back in
`StepResult.events`; `ctx.emit` throws for a payload that fails the schema.

entries.name: defineGame
entries.doc:
Checks a spec and fills in every default over the runtime, the Pixi renderer, Ruken hosting and the default
screens; `startGame` boots the result. Pure: it reads no document, so a game module also loads in Node.
Throws `BootDefect` (its cause a `GameSpecError`) for an invalid spec.

entries.name: definePlugin
entries.doc:
Defines a plugin from a name, its dependencies and its definitions, given in the keyed lists or in one flat
`defs` list sorted by kind. A plugin written either way registers the same lists and gets the same schema
hash. `config` is copied as canonical, frozen JSON, so anything that cannot hash exactly throws a
`CanonicalJsonError` here.

entries.name: defineResource
entries.doc:
Defines a resource by id, schema and starting value. `createSim` parses `init()` with the schema, so a bad
start fails there.

entries.name: defineSave
entries.doc: Declares a save. It checks nothing the SDK checks; it only gives the definition its type.

entries.name: defineSystem
entries.doc:
A system: `defineSystem(name, run)` runs in `gameplay`, `defineSystem(name, phase, run)` in that phase, and the
object form also takes `before`/`after`. All three build the same SystemDef (DX spec §3.2).

entries.name: DrawContext
entries.doc: What `draw` receives each frame. Coordinates are logical playfield pixels (plan D-2).

entries.name: DrawEntity
entries.doc: One entity, read-only: its components' values are frozen copies.

entries.name: DrawSim
entries.doc: The sim at this frame, read-only.

entries.name: DrawTextOptions
entries.doc: Options for `DrawContext.text`: colour and font size.

entries.name: EntityRef
entries.doc: A live entity, addressed by its StableId. Writes are coerced per field type and mark the entity changed.
entries.signature:
interface EntityRef {
  readonly sid: number
  has(component: ComponentDef): boolean
  get<S extends FieldSchema>(component: ComponentDef<S>): Readonly<FieldValues<S>>
  set<S extends FieldSchema>(component: ComponentDef<S>, values: Partial<FieldValues<S>>): void
  add<S extends FieldSchema>(component: ComponentDef<S>, values?: Partial<FieldValues<S>>): void
  remove(component: ComponentDef): void
}

entries.name: EventDef
entries.doc: An event a system emits: an id and the Zod schema its payload must match. Create one with `defineEvent`.

entries.name: GameSaves
entries.doc:
What a game saves, and how the default screens read it from the sim and put it back (M5.2). The title lists the
save's slots; New game writes the starting data, Continue loads a slot, and play keeps it saved while it runs, on
the triggers the `def` declares (autosave).

entries.name: GameSpec
entries.doc:
A game in one object (DX spec §3.1): its id, size and sim, and optionally its title, input, views, sounds,
scores, saves, content, screens, settings, extensions, draw layer and host and renderer options.
`defineGame` fills in every default.

entries.name: GameSpecError
entries.doc: Every invalid field of a spec, by path: `size.width: …`.

entries.name: InputMap
entries.doc: Held keys, touch buttons and gamepad buttons, turned into one command per tick (DX spec §3.3).

entries.name: InputSource
entries.doc: The input map attached to a window for one play session.

entries.name: KeyBindings
entries.doc: By `KeyboardEvent.code`, so the keys sit in the same place on every keyboard layout.
entries.signature: type KeyBindings<Z extends z.ZodType> = Readonly<Record<string, Payload<Z>>>

entries.name: keys
entries.doc:
An input map sending `command` once per tick with the payload of what is held: keys by
`KeyboardEvent.code`, on-screen touch buttons, gamepad buttons, the stick and gestures, merged over the
idle payload. Throws when a binding's payload fails the command's schema, and when a key in `options.required` has
no binding.

entries.name: KeysOptions
entries.doc:
Options for `keys`: touch buttons, gamepad buttons, gestures and the stick, the idle payload, required keys
and the Controls section's labels.

entries.name: PluginDef
entries.doc:
A bundle of definitions the sim registers together: components, commands, events, resources and systems,
the plugins it depends on, and optionally per-sim engine state and `config`. Create one with
`definePlugin`.
entries.signature:
interface PluginDef {
  readonly kind: 'plugin'
  readonly name: string
  /** Creates this plugin's per-sim engine state; its systems see it as `ctx.pluginState`. */
  readonly state: ((setup: PluginStateSetup) => Promise<PluginState>) | undefined
  readonly dependsOn: readonly string[]
  readonly components: readonly ComponentDef[]
  readonly commands: readonly CommandDef[]
  readonly events: readonly EventDef[]
  readonly resources: readonly ResourceDef[]
  readonly systems: readonly SystemDef[]
  /**
   * Settings that change what the plugin simulates (physics gravity), as plain JSON. Part of the schema hash,
   * so a snapshot never restores into a sim configured differently. Undefined when the plugin has none.
   */
  readonly config: unknown
}

entries.name: postFilter
entries.doc:
Declares a screen-space filter over the whole picture: `renderer: { postFilters: [postFilter('vignette', {
glsl, wgsl })] }`. The renderer builds it when it starts and keeps it in the stage's post-filter slot under
`name`. A filter that cannot be built, or whose GLSL does not link, is left out with a warning and the frame
draws without it. Throws when the name or either shader is empty.

entries.name: PostFilterDef
entries.doc: A declared filter, as `postFilter` returns it and `PixiRendererOptions.postFilters` takes it.
entries.signature:
interface PostFilterDef {
  readonly name: string
  readonly glsl: string
  readonly wgsl: string
  readonly order: number
  readonly minTier: QualityTier | undefined
}

entries.name: PostFilterSpec
entries.doc:
What a screen-space filter is made of: the same effect written twice, for WebGL2 (`glsl`) and WebGPU (`wgsl`),
so the two renderers stay at parity. Both are fragment shaders that `filterPrograms` joins to the shared vertex
stage: GLSL reads `vTextureCoord`, `vPixelCoord` and `uTexture`; WGSL has `mainFragment(input: VSOutput)`.

entries.name: rect
entries.doc:
A filled rectangle that follows its component's `x`, `y` and `angle`, interpolated between ticks:
`entityViews: { [Body.id]: rect({ w: 8, h: 8, color: 0xf9c22b }) }`.

entries.name: RectViewOptions
entries.doc: A `rect` view's size, colour and anchor.

entries.name: ResourceDef
entries.doc:
A value the sim keeps once, not on any entity: an id, a Zod schema and the `init` that gives its starting
value. Create one with `defineResource`.

entries.name: SaveDef
entries.doc: A game's save: one record, or a fixed number of slots, each one Ruken key.

entries.name: ScreensGame
entries.doc: What the default screens need from the game.

entries.name: Sim
entries.doc:
A running simulation, stepped with commands, that can snapshot, restore and hash its state. `step` is the
only way gameplay state changes. Create one with `createSim`, and `dispose` it when done.

entries.name: SimContext
entries.doc: What a system's `run` receives each tick (spec §4.1).

entries.name: sprite
entries.doc:
A sprite that follows its component's `x`, `y` and `angle`, interpolated between ticks. `source` is a
texture or a url: a url the runtime already loaded (it is in `Assets.cache`) shows at once; otherwise the
sprite is empty until `Assets.load` resolves. A url that fails to load is reported with `reportError`
and the sprite stays empty. The frame textures are sliced once per factory and shared by its sprites.
With `frame`, the url is an atlas page's Spritesheet and the sprite shows that frame; a name the atlas lacks
is reported the same way.

entries.name: SpriteFrames
entries.doc:
The texture is a sheet of equal frames, read left to right, top to bottom. The pose component's numeric
`frame` field picks one (floored, wrapped by the frame count); with no `frame` field the first is shown.
Frames switch on ticks; they are not interpolated.

entries.name: SpriteViewOptions
entries.doc: A `sprite` view's anchor and either its sprite-sheet frames or one frame of a packed atlas.

entries.name: startGame
entries.doc:
Boots a game (DX spec §3.1): `defineGame`'s defaults over the runtime, the Pixi renderer, Ruken hosting
and the default screens, then the runtime's boot on the game's root. Takes a spec or a game `defineGame`
already returned. Throws `BootDefect` before anything mounts when the spec is invalid or there is no
root (`spec.root`, else `#game`); a failure after that shows on the runtime's boot failure panel.

entries.name: StepResult
entries.doc:
What one `step` produced: the new tick, the events emitted, the renderer's delta and the commands that were
rejected.

entries.name: SystemDef
entries.doc:
A system: a name, the phase it runs in, the systems it must run `before` or `after` within that phase, and
its `run`, called once per tick. Create one with `defineSystem`.
entries.signature:
interface SystemDef {
  readonly kind: 'system'
  readonly name: string
  readonly phase: Phase
  readonly before: readonly string[]
  readonly after: readonly string[]
  readonly run: (ctx: SimContext) => void
}

entries.name: TouchButton
entries.doc: One on-screen touch button: every key bound to the same payload shares it.

entries.name: AssetsSource
entries.doc:
What `content/assets.toml` says: for each screen, the files it waits for (`dir/*` names every file in a
folder), and the atlases and fonts of the asset build it uses, by their names in `atlases.toml` and
`fonts.toml`. A preloaded screen's atlas pages and font subsets join the preload list (M5.6F.2).

entries.name: buildContent
entries.doc: Compiles, writes every output under the output folder, then removes the outputs it no longer produces.
entries.signature: const buildContent: (options: ContentOptions) => Effect.Effect<CompiledContent, ContentCompileFailed | InvalidContentConfig | ContentWriteFailed>;

entries.name: checkTuningLayer
entries.doc:
Checks one layer of tuning against code-owned declarations. `complete` is true for the base layer, which
must name every tunable; false for a partial override (FloorFifty's stage and mode layers).

Invariants are rejected before unknown names so the more specific answer wins, then non-numbers, then
integer declarations, then the inclusive range.

entries.name: compileContent
entries.doc: Compiles `<root>/content` in memory. Writes nothing.
entries.signature: const compileContent: (options: ContentOptions) => Effect.Effect<CompiledContent, ContentCompileFailed | InvalidContentConfig>;

entries.name: CompiledContent
entries.doc:
The result of a compile: the content and its hash, the sim partition, every output file's text, warnings,
the languages and each language's message catalog.

entries.name: ContentCompileFailed
entries.doc: The authored content has problems. Every one is listed, sorted; nothing was written.
entries.signature: class ContentCompileFailed extends CompileFailedBase {}

entries.name: ContentConfig
entries.doc: The default export of `automata.content.ts`.

entries.name: ContentData
entries.doc: The compiled content as it is written to `content.json` and hashed.
entries.signature: type ContentData = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

entries.name: ContentGenerator
entries.doc:
A generator: a unique name and a pure `generate` that turns compiled content into extra files. Create one
with `defineContentGenerator`.

entries.name: contentHash
entries.doc: 16 lowercase hex digits.
entries.signature: function contentHash(data: unknown): string;

entries.name: ContentOptions
entries.doc:
What the content compiler is given: the project root, the registered kinds, and optionally tunables,
invariants, flow capabilities, generators, an output folder and Paraglide.

entries.name: contentRef
entries.doc: The ID of another content item of `kind`. Checked to exist, and to be that kind, after parsing.
entries.signature: function contentRef<const K extends string>(kind: K): z.ZodType<string, string>;

entries.name: ContentSchemaDef
entries.doc:
A content kind a game registers: its name, the Zod schema each item must match, where its TOML files live,
and whether the sim receives it. Create one with `defineContentSchema`.

entries.name: ContentSchemaOptions
entries.doc: Options for `defineContentSchema`; `sim: false` keeps the kind out of the sim's content and its hash.

entries.name: ContentSchemaPlace
entries.doc: Where a kind's files are: every TOML file under a folder (a collection), or one file (a document).

entries.name: ContentWriteFailed
entries.doc: An output could not be written. Files already replaced are whole; none is half written.
entries.signature: class ContentWriteFailed extends WriteFailedBase {}

entries.name: DEFAULT_OUT_DIR
entries.doc: Where outputs go when `outDir` is not set: `content/generated`, relative to the project root.
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = "content/generated";

entries.name: DEFAULT_PALETTE
entries.doc: The palette a game gets when it has no `content/palette.toml`: Endesga 64.
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_PALETTE: Palette;

entries.name: defineContentGenerator
entries.doc:
Defines a generator by name and `generate` function. Generators do no I/O: the compiler writes their files.
A generator that throws, repeats another's name, returns a path outside the output folder or writes a file
another generator wrote is reported as `InvalidContentConfig`.
entries.signature: function defineContentGenerator(name: string, generate: (input: GeneratorInput) => GeneratorOutput): ContentGenerator;

entries.name: defineContentSchema
entries.doc:
Registers a content kind: a name, its Zod schema, and a folder (every TOML file in it is an item) or one
file (a single document). The sim receives the kind unless `{ sim: false }`. A bad registration (a name
that does not start with a lower-case letter followed by lower-case letters, digits and dashes, a built-in
name, a duplicate, or a place two kinds share) is reported when content compiles, as `InvalidContentConfig`.
entries.signature: function defineContentSchema<const K extends string, S extends z.ZodType>(kind: K, schema: S, place: ContentSchemaPlace, options?: ContentSchemaOptions): ContentSchemaDef<K, S>;

entries.name: Diagnostic
entries.doc:
One authoring problem: a stable `code`, the file to open, the 1-based line and column, the dotted key
inside it and a message that says what to write instead.

entries.name: DiagnosticCode
entries.doc: Stable codes. Tests and tools match on these, so a code is never renamed, only added.
entries.signature: type DiagnosticCode = "invalidToml" | "invalidType" | "missingField" | "unknownField" | "invalidId" | "unknownReference" | "wrongKind" | "outOfRange" | "invariantNotAuthorable" | "invalidFlow" | "invalidPalette" | "invalidGame" | "missingAsset" | "invalidAsset" | "offPalette" | "missingGlyph" | "duplicateMessageKey" | "staleTranslation" | "staleArtifact" | "reservedKey" | "simReference" | "skippedFile";

entries.name: FlowCapabilities
entries.doc: What the game's code implements: the screens, and optionally the pairs and destinations each allows.

entries.name: FlowGraph
entries.doc:
The checked screen flow from `flow.toml`: the entry screen, every screen, the terminal screens and every
transition, in a fixed order.

entries.name: FlowTransition
entries.doc:
One checked move in the flow: on `event` the game goes `from` one screen `to` another, drawn in the
`transition` style (`cut` when unwritten).

entries.name: formatDiagnostic
entries.doc: `content/tuning.toml:12:1  GRAVITY  outOfRange: expected -1200..-100, received -2000`
entries.signature: function formatDiagnostic(d: Diagnostic): string;

entries.name: GameSource
entries.doc:
What `content/game.toml` says about the game: its source language, rating, content descriptors, estimated
hours, the analytics events it may send, and the screens whose files are preloaded.

entries.name: GeneratorInput
entries.doc:
Everything a generator is given: the compiled content and its hash, the sim partition, the registered
schemas, the message catalog and the tuning metadata.

entries.name: GeneratorOutput
entries.doc: What a generator returns: files to write and diagnostics to report. Both are optional.

entries.name: InvalidContentConfig
entries.doc: The game's code registered something unusable (a duplicate kind, a clashing generator).
entries.signature: class InvalidContentConfig extends InvalidConfigBase {}

entries.name: localized
entries.doc: Text a player reads, written in the source language. It gets a message key for translators.
entries.signature: function localized(): z.ZodType<string, string>;

entries.name: MessageCatalog
entries.doc: One locale's messages: message key to translated text.
entries.signature: type MessageCatalog = Readonly<Record<string, string>>;

entries.name: messageKey
entries.doc: The message key of one text. `id` is absent for a single-document kind.
entries.signature: function messageKey(kind: string, id: string | undefined, path: DataPath): string;

entries.name: MessageLocation
entries.doc: A message's place in its file, 1-based.

entries.name: Palette
entries.doc: The game's palette: a name and its colors.

entries.name: ParaglideOptions
entries.doc: Where and which catalogs `ContentOptions.paraglide` compiles with Paraglide on build.

entries.name: PreloadInput
entries.doc:
What `preloadList` reads: the content options (to compile `game.toml` and `assets.toml`, and to find the asset
build's outputs below `outDir`) and the built game folder.

entries.name: preloadList
entries.doc:
The files Ruken preloads before the game starts, in order, for `[loading] preload`: each `preload_screens`
screen's files from `assets.toml` (the flow's entry when none is named), then the pages of the atlases and
every language's subset of the fonts it names there, which `automata-content assets` wrote below `outDir`
and the build serves in `atlases/` and `fonts/`; without repeats. Empty without a `game.toml`. Fails with
`ContentCompileFailed` carrying a diagnostic for every file the build lacks (`missingAsset`), every atlas or
font not declared (`unknownReference`) or not built (`missingAsset`), all at once, or with
`InvalidContentConfig`.
entries.signature: const preloadList: (input: PreloadInput) => Effect.Effect<string[], ContentCompileFailed | InvalidContentConfig>;

entries.name: renderTuningTable
entries.doc: Every tunable once, sorted by name, with its type, range and value in `content/tuning.toml`.
entries.signature: function renderTuningTable(meta: TuningMeta): string;

entries.name: RukenFields
entries.doc:
The `[content]` and `[analytics]` tables of Ruken's manifest, worked out from `game.toml` and the languages
present and written to `ruken-fields.json`.
entries.signature: type RukenFields = Pick<Manifest, "content" | "analytics">;

entries.name: SimPartition
entries.doc:
The part of the compiled content the sim receives (`tuning` and every kind with `sim: true`) and its hash,
which gates snapshots and replays.

entries.name: sortDiagnostics
entries.doc:
Returns the diagnostics in the one fixed order (file, line, column, key, code, message), without changing
the input. The order never depends on locale.
entries.signature: function sortDiagnostics(diagnostics: readonly Diagnostic[]): Diagnostic[];

entries.name: TunableDeclaration
entries.doc:
A tunable a game declares in code: `int` or `float`, an inclusive range and a default. Content selects a
value inside the range and never widens it.

entries.name: TunableDeclarations
entries.doc: A game's tunables by name (upper-case words joined by underscores, such as `GRAVITY`).
entries.signature: type TunableDeclarations = Readonly<Record<string, TunableDeclaration>>;

entries.name: TuningMeta
entries.doc:
Every tunable's type, value and range (`min`, `max`, `step`) by name, as written to `tuning-meta.json` for
debug sliders.
entries.signature: type TuningMeta = Readonly<Record<string, TuningEntryMeta>>;

entries.name: verifyContent
entries.doc: Fails with `staleArtifact` for each committed output that differs from a fresh compile.
entries.signature: const verifyContent: (options: ContentOptions) => Effect.Effect<void, ContentCompileFailed | InvalidContentConfig>;

entries.name: withTuningTable
entries.doc: The guide with its generated section replaced, or undefined when it has no markers.
entries.signature: function withTuningTable(guide: string, meta: TuningMeta): string | undefined;

entries.name: ATLAS_EXTRUDE
entries.doc: Pixels of each frame's edge repeated around it, so filtering never samples a neighbour.
entries.signature: const ATLAS_EXTRUDE = 1;

entries.name: ATLAS_PADDING
entries.doc: Transparent pixels between cells, and between a cell and the page edge.
entries.signature: const ATLAS_PADDING = 1;

entries.name: ATLAS_PAGE_MAX
entries.doc: The largest atlas page side, in pixels: WebGL2's guaranteed `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`.
entries.signature: const ATLAS_PAGE_MAX = 2048;

entries.name: AtlasFrameTooLarge
entries.doc: A frame that cannot fit a page even alone.

entries.name: AtlasOutputs
entries.doc: What `buildAtlases` produces; the caller writes it.

entries.name: buildAtlases
entries.doc:
Builds every atlas `<root>/content/atlases.toml` names, or fails with every problem found. Without the file
there is nothing to build.
entries.signature: const buildAtlases: (root: string) => Effect.Effect<AtlasOutputs, ContentCompileFailed>;

entries.name: buildFonts
entries.doc:
Builds every subset `<root>/content/fonts.toml` names, or fails with every problem found. Without the file
there is nothing to build, and the content is not compiled.
entries.signature: const buildFonts: (options: ContentOptions) => Effect.Effect<FontOutputs, ContentCompileFailed | InvalidContentConfig>;

entries.name: fontCoverage
entries.doc: Whether a font file (TrueType, OpenType, woff or woff2) has a glyph for each character.
entries.signature: function fontCoverage(font: Uint8Array): (character: string) => boolean;

entries.name: FontOutputs
entries.doc: What `buildFonts` produces; the caller writes it.

entries.name: FontsFile
entries.doc: `content/fonts.toml`: each source font by name.

entries.name: FontSource
entries.doc: One source font: its committed file, the sha256 of its bytes, its licence and the languages it serves.

entries.name: FrameSize
entries.doc: A frame to pack: its name (the PNG's file name without `.png`) and size in pixels.

entries.name: PackedAtlas
entries.doc: Every frame's placement, and the pages they fill.

entries.name: packFrames
entries.doc: Packs `frames` into atlas pages. Throws `AtlasFrameTooLarge` for a frame no page can hold.
entries.signature: function packFrames(frames: readonly FrameSize[]): PackedAtlas;

entries.name: Placement
entries.doc: Where a frame's own pixels are: inside its extrusion, on page `page`.

entries.name: subsetWoff2
entries.doc: The font cut to `characters`, as woff2. A character the font lacks is simply not in the subset.
entries.signature: function subsetWoff2(source: Uint8Array, characters: ReadonlySet<string>): Promise<Uint8Array>;

entries.name: ALWAYS_CHARACTERS
entries.doc: Printable ASCII, CJK symbols and punctuation, half- and full-width forms, and the symbols the UI draws.
entries.signature: const ALWAYS_CHARACTERS: readonly string[];

entries.name: catalogCharacters
entries.doc: Every character the catalog's messages show. `$schema` is the file's format, not text a player reads.
entries.signature: function catalogCharacters(catalog: MessageCatalog): Set<string>;

entries.name: ContentText
entries.doc: `text(kind, id, path, authored, inputs?)`: the text in the active locale, or the authored text.
entries.signature: type ContentText = (kind: string, id: string | undefined, path: DataPath, authored: string, inputs?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>) => string;

entries.name: ContentTextOptions
entries.doc: Options for `createContentText`.

entries.name: createContentText
entries.doc: A lookup over the messages module Paraglide compiles into `paraglide.outdir` (its `messages.js`, imported whole).
entries.signature: function createContentText(messages: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, options?: ContentTextOptions): ContentText;

entries.name: endonymOf
entries.doc:
A language's name in its own language ("日本語" for `ja`), from the browser's `Intl.DisplayNames`. An engine without
it, or a tag it cannot name, gives the tag back, so the picker never shows nothing.
entries.signature: function endonymOf(tag: string): string;

entries.name: hasRawText
entries.doc:
True when a piece of visible text has English in it that did not come from the xx-long catalog: any ASCII
letter outside a ⟦ ⟧ span. Data a player typed (a name) is also "raw", so a check lists the data it expects.
entries.signature: function hasRawText(text: string): boolean;

entries.name: localeCharacters
entries.doc:
A locale's own characters for its subset font: `ALWAYS_CHARACTERS` and the catalog's characters. The font build
also adds every content language's name for the language picker (`endonymOf`, M5.5F).
entries.signature: function localeCharacters(catalog: MessageCatalog): Set<string>;

entries.name: MessageCatalog
entries.doc: One locale's messages: message key to translated text.
entries.signature: type MessageCatalog = Readonly<Record<string, string>>;

entries.name: messageKey
entries.doc: The message key of one text. `id` is absent for a single-document kind.
entries.signature: function messageKey(kind: string, id: string | undefined, path: DataPath): string;

entries.name: MessageValue
entries.doc: A value in an inlang message file: a message, a list of variants, or a namespace or variant object.

entries.name: PSEUDO_LOCALE
entries.doc: The pseudo-locale's tag. `Intl` reads it as the unknown language `xx`, so formatting falls back, never throws.
entries.signature: const PSEUDO_LOCALE = "xx-long";

entries.name: pseudoLocalize
entries.doc:
The xx-long form of one message string. Placeholders and escaped braces stay as written. The extra length is
spread over the words in proportion to their length, each word's share right after it, so a long message keeps
the places a line can break, as a longer language's would; a message with no words has it at the end.
entries.signature: function pseudoLocalize(message: string): string;

entries.name: pseudoMessages
entries.doc:
The xx-long form of a whole message file (the inlang message format): nested namespaces are walked, plural
variants keep their `declarations` and `selectors` (they are code, not text) and only their `match` texts
change. `$schema` is copied as is.

entries.name: snakeKey
entries.doc: `snow-shrine` → `snow_shrine`, `fastFall` → `fast_fall`, `melee/sword` → `melee_sword`.
entries.signature: function snakeKey(value: string): string;

entries.name: automataContent
entries.doc:
The Vite plugin that compiles content and serves it as `virtual:automata/content`. It builds when Vite
starts and on every save in dev, with the same build as `automata-content build`. A `vite build` with
content errors fails; a dev server keeps serving the last good content and reports the diagnostics through
Vite's logger and the `automata:content-error` event (`automata:content` after a good save). It also sets
`build.assetsInlineLimit: 0` when the game's config leaves it unset, so no asset becomes a `data:` URL that Ruken's
CSP refuses to fetch.
entries.signature: function automataContent(pluginOptions?: AutomataContentOptions): Plugin;

entries.name: AutomataContentOptions
entries.doc: The plugin's options: `ContentOptions`, with `root` defaulting to Vite's root.

entries.name: VIRTUAL_MODULE_ID
entries.doc: The import path of the compiled content: `content`, `contentHash`, `simContent` and `simContentHash`.
entries.signature: const VIRTUAL_MODULE_ID = "virtual:automata/content";

entries.name: AutosavePolicy
entries.doc:
When the loaded slot writes itself: on each listed trigger, with `intervalSeconds` for the `interval`
timer.

entries.name: AutosaveTrigger
entries.doc: What can make the loaded slot write itself (M5 spec §4.4).
entries.signature: type AutosaveTrigger = 'screen-exit' | 'round-end' | 'background' | 'interval'

entries.name: Camera2d
entries.doc:
A presentation-only 2D camera over one container: it follows a target, shakes, and writes only that
container's transform, never a sim value.

entries.name: Camera2dOptions
entries.doc: How `createCamera2d` frames the world: the view's size, and optionally a follow, bounds and zoom.

entries.name: CameraRect
entries.doc: A world-space rectangle, in logical px: `Camera2dOptions.bounds`.

entries.name: createCamera2d
entries.doc:
A camera writing `stage`'s transform (usually `PixiStage.world`). `seed` fixes the shake's random sequence,
so a shake looks the same in every run and visual test.

entries.name: defaultContent
entries.doc: The default flow `title → play ⇄ paused → title`, with `paused ⇄ settings` (M4.4), and its hash.
entries.signature: function defaultContent(): GameContent;

entries.name: defaultScreens
entries.doc:
The title, play, paused and settings screens (DX spec §7, M4.4) over the default content's flow
(`title → play ⇄ paused → title`, `paused ⇄ settings`).

The screens share one sim: play creates it on first entry (seed, plugins, content, then `setup`),
paused keeps it, and the title drops it, so Quit to title and Play start again at tick 0. A runtime that shuts
down with the sim alive drops it too, whichever screen is current (DX.2c). Returning
from paused re-sends the whole state to the renderer (G-5): `AppLoop.run` resets the renderer, so
play restores the sim's own snapshot, which makes the next step a resync.
entries.signature: function defaultScreens(game: ScreensGame): ScreenDef[];

entries.name: DefinedGame
entries.doc: The runtime's `GameDefinition`, plus what the screens and the golden replay read from the spec.

entries.name: defineGame
entries.doc:
Checks a spec and fills in every default over the runtime, the Pixi renderer, Ruken hosting and the default
screens; `startGame` boots the result. Pure: it reads no document, so a game module also loads in Node.
Throws `BootDefect` (its cause a `GameSpecError`) for an invalid spec.
entries.signature: function defineGame<S = never, D = unknown>(spec: GameSpec<S, D>): DefinedGame<S>;

entries.name: defineSave
entries.doc: Declares a save. It checks nothing the SDK checks; it only gives the definition its type.

entries.name: DrawContext
entries.doc: What `draw` receives each frame. Coordinates are logical playfield pixels (plan D-2).

entries.name: DrawEntity
entries.doc: One entity, read-only: its components' values are frozen copies.

entries.name: DrawSim
entries.doc: The sim at this frame, read-only.

entries.name: DrawTextOptions
entries.doc: Options for `DrawContext.text`: colour and font size.

entries.name: GameSaves
entries.doc:
What a game saves, and how the default screens read it from the sim and put it back (M5.2). The title lists the
save's slots; New game writes the starting data, Continue loads a slot, and play keeps it saved while it runs, on
the triggers the `def` declares (autosave).

entries.name: GameSpec
entries.doc:
A game in one object (DX spec §3.1): its id, size and sim, and optionally its title, input, views, sounds,
scores, saves, content, screens, settings, extensions, draw layer and host and renderer options.
`defineGame` fills in every default.

entries.name: GameSpecError
entries.doc: Every invalid field of a spec, by path: `size.width: …`.

entries.name: InputMap
entries.doc: Held keys, touch buttons and gamepad buttons, turned into one command per tick (DX spec §3.3).

entries.name: InputSource
entries.doc: The input map attached to a window for one play session.

entries.name: KeyBindings
entries.doc: By `KeyboardEvent.code`, so the keys sit in the same place on every keyboard layout.
entries.signature: type KeyBindings<Z extends z.ZodType> = Readonly<Record<string, Payload<Z>>>;

entries.name: keys
entries.doc:
An input map sending `command` once per tick with the payload of what is held: keys by
`KeyboardEvent.code`, on-screen touch buttons, gamepad buttons, the stick and gestures, merged over the
idle payload. Throws when a binding's payload fails the command's schema, and when a key in `options.required` has
no binding.
entries.signature: function keys<Z extends z.ZodType>(command: CommandDef<Z>, bindings: KeyBindings<Z>, options?: KeysOptions<Z>): InputMap;

entries.name: KeysOptions
entries.doc:
Options for `keys`: touch buttons, gamepad buttons, gestures and the stick, the idle payload, required keys
and the Controls section's labels.

entries.name: postFilter
entries.doc:
Declares a screen-space filter over the whole picture: `renderer: { postFilters: [postFilter('vignette', {
glsl, wgsl })] }`. The renderer builds it when it starts and keeps it in the stage's post-filter slot under
`name`. A filter that cannot be built, or whose GLSL does not link, is left out with a warning and the frame
draws without it. Throws when the name or either shader is empty.

entries.name: PostFilterDef
entries.doc: A declared filter, as `postFilter` returns it and `PixiRendererOptions.postFilters` takes it.
entries.signature:
interface PostFilterDef {
  readonly name: string
  readonly glsl: string
  readonly wgsl: string
  readonly order: number
  readonly minTier: QualityTier | undefined
}

entries.name: PostFilterSpec
entries.doc:
What a screen-space filter is made of: the same effect written twice, for WebGL2 (`glsl`) and WebGPU (`wgsl`),
so the two renderers stay at parity. Both are fragment shaders that `filterPrograms` joins to the shared vertex
stage: GLSL reads `vTextureCoord`, `vPixelCoord` and `uTexture`; WGSL has `mainFragment(input: VSOutput)`.

entries.name: rect
entries.doc:
A filled rectangle that follows its component's `x`, `y` and `angle`, interpolated between ticks:
`entityViews: { [Body.id]: rect({ w: 8, h: 8, color: 0xf9c22b }) }`.

entries.name: RectViewOptions
entries.doc: A `rect` view's size, colour and anchor.

entries.name: SaveDef
entries.doc: A game's save: one record, or a fixed number of slots, each one Ruken key.

entries.name: ScreensGame
entries.doc: What the default screens need from the game.

entries.name: sprite
entries.doc:
A sprite that follows its component's `x`, `y` and `angle`, interpolated between ticks. `source` is a
texture or a url: a url the runtime already loaded (it is in `Assets.cache`) shows at once; otherwise the
sprite is empty until `Assets.load` resolves. A url that fails to load is reported with `reportError`
and the sprite stays empty. The frame textures are sliced once per factory and shared by its sprites.
With `frame`, the url is an atlas page's Spritesheet and the sprite shows that frame; a name the atlas lacks
is reported the same way.

entries.name: SpriteFrames
entries.doc:
The texture is a sheet of equal frames, read left to right, top to bottom. The pose component's numeric
`frame` field picks one (floored, wrapped by the frame count); with no `frame` field the first is shown.
Frames switch on ticks; they are not interpolated.

entries.name: SpriteViewOptions
entries.doc: A `sprite` view's anchor and either its sprite-sheet frames or one frame of a packed atlas.

entries.name: startGame
entries.doc:
Boots a game (DX spec §3.1): `defineGame`'s defaults over the runtime, the Pixi renderer, Ruken hosting
and the default screens, then the runtime's boot on the game's root. Takes a spec or a game `defineGame`
already returned. Throws `BootDefect` before anything mounts when the spec is invalid or there is no
root (`spec.root`, else `#game`); a failure after that shows on the runtime's boot failure panel.
entries.signature: function startGame<S = never>(game: GameSpec<S> | DefinedGame<S>): RuntimeHandle;

entries.name: TouchButton
entries.doc: One on-screen touch button: every key bound to the same payload shares it.

entries.name: isDefinedGame
entries.doc: Whether `value` came from `defineGame`.
entries.signature: function isDefinedGame<S>(value: GameSpec<S> | DefinedGame<S>): value is DefinedGame<S>;

entries.name: AnalyticsProps
entries.doc:
The properties of one analytics event: flat names to strings, numbers or booleans, as the Ruken SDK accepts
them.
entries.signature: type AnalyticsProps = Record<string, string | number | boolean>;

entries.name: ErrorCode
entries.doc: Ruken's error codes (`@ruken/protocol` `ERROR_CODES`), as the SDK's `RukenError` carries them.
entries.signature: type ErrorCode = RukenError["code"];

entries.name: findRukenSdkMarkers
entries.doc: The markers found in `code` (built JavaScript), each named once; empty means no Ruken SDK code.
entries.signature: function findRukenSdkMarkers(code: string): string[];

entries.name: HOST_EXIT_CAP
entries.doc:
How long the game may hold the host's close (FloorFifty `ruken/exit.ts`,
Ruken P6 §4 "1 s cap"). Ruken's own grace is 1.5 s
(`sdk-host/src/bridge/defaults.ts` `EXIT_GRACE_MS`), so the game always
answers before the host gives up on it.
entries.signature: const HOST_EXIT_CAP: Duration.Duration;

entries.name: HostError
entries.doc: Any failure after the handshake. A request that fails never falls back to another path.
entries.signature: class HostError extends HostErrorBase {}

entries.name: HostHandshakeFailed
entries.doc:
The page is inside a frame, but the SDK got no usable welcome and fell back
to its standalone session. Not fatal: reported on `Hosting.handshake.fellBack`
and logged once (shared contracts §1.2).
entries.signature: class HostHandshakeFailed extends HostHandshakeFailedBase {}

entries.name: Hosting
entries.doc:
Everything a game may ask of, or hear from, its host: the `Hosting` contract
of the M1 shared contracts spec §1, implemented by the host lane.
The `Hosting` service tag.

entries.name: HostingLeaderboards
entries.doc:
The host's leaderboards (Ruken's `LeaderboardsApi`, PRODUCT spec §2 F1). Needs the `leaderboards` grant.
Each call relays the SDK's answer or error as a `HostError`: without the grant and standalone it fails
`UNSUPPORTED`, offline it fails with the host's code. None keeps a local board instead.

entries.name: HostingLive
entries.doc: The single `Hosting` layer for games (shared contracts §1.1).
entries.signature: function HostingLive(options: HostingOptions, seams?: HostingSeams): Layer.Layer<Hosting, HostError>;

entries.name: HostingOptions
entries.doc: What the game asks of its host. In M1 the game passes these by hand; later they come from content.

entries.name: HostingSaves
entries.doc: The player's saves (shared contracts §1.1). Each call relays the SDK's error as a `HostError`; none falls back.

entries.name: HostingSeams
entries.doc: Test seams. Games pass nothing; `HostingTest` passes the fake host's in-memory window pair.

entries.name: makeHosting
entries.doc:
Builds `Hosting` over `Ruken.init`. The SDK decides between a hosted session
and its standalone one (shared contracts §1.1), enforces grants and limits,
and owns the handshake's timing; AF relays what it reports.

When the scope closes, in this order: Hosting marks itself closed (later
calls fail with `HostError{code:'CANCELLED'}`), every observed stream ends,
and then the session is disposed.
entries.signature: function makeHosting(options: HostingOptions, seams?: HostingSeams): Effect.Effect<Hosting, HostError, Scope.Scope>;

entries.name: RUKEN_SDK_MARKERS
entries.doc:
String literals only the Ruken SDK contains, which survive minification (PUB spec §3): the SDK's storage probe
key (`env-browser.ts`) and its standalone refusal message (`standalone.ts`), at RukenApp d0fa2fe (as at
b30d31b). An `itch` or `web` build must contain neither, because it bundles the web adapter instead of the SDK;
a `ruken` build contains both. The web adapter's own probe key (`WEB_STORAGE_PROBE_KEY`) is deliberately different.

Re-check these after re-vendoring the SDK: `target.build.test.ts` fails if a default build stops containing them.
entries.signature: const RUKEN_SDK_MARKERS: readonly string[];

entries.name: toHostError
entries.doc:
Turns whatever the SDK threw or rejected with into a `HostError`.
- A `RukenError` keeps its code and retryable flag.
- A `QuotaExceededError` is what Ruken's save map throws for a save over a
  limit (`sdk/src/save-map.ts`); it becomes `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, which Ruken
  marks not retryable.
- Anything else (a closed port, a bug) becomes `INTERNAL`, which Ruken marks retryable.
entries.signature: function toHostError(operation: string, cause: unknown): HostError;

entries.name: FakeHostClock
entries.doc: The clock shape `@ruken/sdk-host`'s fake host takes; the game's `SdkEnv.timers` run on it too.

entries.name: FakeHostHandle
entries.doc: The fake host behind `HostingTest`, for tests that drive the host side.

entries.name: HostingTest
entries.doc:
`HostingLive` wired to `@ruken/sdk-host`'s fake host over in-memory ports,
with the real SDK in between (shared contracts §1.1). Provides `Hosting` and
`FakeHostHandle`; both are disposed when the scope closes.
entries.signature: function HostingTest(options?: HostingTestOptions): Layer.Layer<Hosting | FakeHostHandle, HostError>;

entries.name: HostingTestOptions
entries.doc:
What to change about `HostingTest`'s defaults: the game's hosting options, the fake host, the SDK
environment and the game's origin.

entries.name: manualClock
entries.doc:
SDK and fake-host timing (hello retries, the 10 s handshake give-up, request
timeouts) runs on this clock, so a test can step past them without waiting
(shared contracts §1.4). AF's own timing uses Effect's `TestClock` instead.
Timers fire in due order; a timer scheduled by another one fires in the same
`advance` if it falls due within it.
entries.signature: function manualClock(startMs?: number): ManualClock;

entries.name: ManualClock
entries.doc:
A clock that moves only when the test calls `advance`. It is both the fake
host's `BridgeClock` (`epochMs`) and the SDK's `SdkTimers` (`now`), so one
clock drives both sides (shared contracts §1.4).

entries.name: realClock
entries.doc: Real time, for tests that only need the host to answer.
entries.signature: const realClock: FakeHostClock;

entries.name: runScoped
entries.doc: Runs a test program in a fresh scope, closing it (and every layer built inside) at the end.
entries.signature: function runScoped<A, E>(program: Effect.Effect<A, E, Scope.Scope>): Promise<A>;

entries.name: TEST_GAME_ORIGIN
entries.doc: The origin `HostingTest` serves the game from unless `gameOrigin` says otherwise.
entries.signature: const TEST_GAME_ORIGIN = "http://localhost:4400";

entries.name: FileError
entries.doc: Reading, writing, listing or removing a file failed.

entries.name: Files
entries.doc:
The service's tag. A tag and an identity interface instead of `class Files extends Context.Tag(...)`, because
isolatedDeclarations cannot type a call in an `extends` clause (the pattern `host`'s `Hosting` uses).

entries.name: FilesLive
entries.doc:
`Files` on `node:fs`: synchronous calls wrapped in `Effect.try`, so the first failure surfaces as a
`FileError`.
entries.signature: const FilesLive: Layer.Layer<Files>;

entries.name: FilesService
entries.doc:
The file operations build-time code needs, each as an Effect. A failed call fails with a `FileError` naming
the path, except `exists`, which cannot fail.

entries.name: ProcessError
entries.doc: A program could not be started (not found, not executable). A non-zero exit is not this error.

entries.name: ProcessRunner
entries.doc: The service's tag; see `Files` for why it is not a `Context.Tag` class.

entries.name: ProcessRunnerLive
entries.doc:
`ProcessRunner` on `node:child_process`: the real programs, with the parent's environment plus
`RunOptions.env`.
entries.signature: const ProcessRunnerLive: Layer.Layer<ProcessRunner>;

entries.name: ProcessRunnerService
entries.doc:
Runs a program with arguments and no shell. The effect fails with a `ProcessError` only when the program
cannot be started; interrupting it stops the program.

entries.name: RunOptions
entries.doc:
How a program is started: its working folder, extra environment, stdin, and whether its output is also
echoed.

entries.name: RunResult
entries.doc:
What a finished program left: its exit code (128 when a signal killed it) and everything it wrote to stdout
and stderr, decoded as UTF-8. A non-zero exit code is a result, not a failure.

entries.name: TaggedErrorClass
entries.doc:
The class `Data.TaggedError(tag)` returns, written out. isolatedDeclarations cannot infer the type of a call in
an `extends` clause, so each error extends a constant annotated with this type instead (the pattern of
`content`'s compile errors and `host`'s errors). `ship` uses it for its own errors.

entries.name: Camera2d
entries.doc:
A presentation-only 2D camera over one container: it follows a target, shakes, and writes only that
container's transform, never a sim value.

entries.name: Camera2dOptions
entries.doc: How `createCamera2d` frames the world: the view's size, and optionally a follow, bounds and zoom.

entries.name: CameraRect
entries.doc: A world-space rectangle, in logical px: `Camera2dOptions.bounds`.

entries.name: canvasResolutionFor
entries.doc:
Calculates device pixels per CSS pixel for the canvas.

Capped at 2 on phones and desktop, and lower at a lower quality tier. A tablet held upright draws at 1x
because its large CSS area would exceed the mobile fragment fill budget at 2x.
entries.signature: function canvasResolutionFor(formFactor: FormFactor, devicePixelRatio: number, tier?: QualityTier): number;

entries.name: CompositeTarget
entries.doc:
The fixed-resolution composite (M4 spec §4.11).

The world and the UI draw here first, at resolution 1 and exactly the play field's logical size, and the result is
nearest-upscaled into the letterbox. Two reasons, and the second is the durable one. Filters cost per pixel, and a
device-resolution frame on a phone is several times the work; bounding the chain to the logical size makes the
cost the same everywhere. More importantly, pixel art sampled at a fractional device scale is pixel art with torn
edges, so compositing at 1:1 and upscaling by whole pixels is correct whatever the cost.

From FloorFifty `apps/client/src/systems/render/render-target.ts` at `ac72660`; FloorFifty's fixed 960 × 540 is
the game's logical size here.

entries.name: createCamera2d
entries.doc:
A camera writing `stage`'s transform (usually `PixiStage.world`). `seed` fixes the shake's random sequence,
so a shake looks the same in every run and visual test.
entries.signature: function createCamera2d(stage: Container, options: Camera2dOptions, seed?: number): Camera2d;

entries.name: createPixiRenderer
entries.doc:
The core 2D renderer (ADR 0002) as a runtime `RendererFactory`: a letterboxed Pixi app on the render
target, entity views from each step's render delta, interpolated each frame. Fails with
`RendererUnavailable` when the renderer cannot start.
entries.signature: function createPixiRenderer(options?: PixiRendererOptions): (target: RenderTarget) => Effect.Effect<PixiRenderer, RendererUnavailable, Scope.Scope>;

entries.name: createPostFilterSlot
entries.doc: A post-filter slot writing its composed filters to `target`'s `filters`.
entries.signature: function createPostFilterSlot(target: PostFilterTarget): PostFilterSlot;

entries.name: DEFAULT_BAR_COLOR
entries.doc: The letterbox bars' default colour (FloorFifty's plum black).
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_BAR_COLOR = 3023407;

entries.name: DEFAULT_BAR_FRACTION
entries.doc: How much of the playfield's height each letterbox bar crops in a landscape view, by default (5%).
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_BAR_FRACTION = .05;

entries.name: DEFAULT_FIELD_COLOR
entries.doc: The default colour behind the playfield, under the world.
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_FIELD_COLOR = 0;

entries.name: EntityView
entries.doc:
What an entity view factory returns: the container drawn for one entity, updated with its current and
previous component values and the interpolation alpha, and destroyed when the entity goes.

entries.name: EntityViewFactory
entries.doc:
Builds the view for one entity, or `undefined` to draw nothing. A record resolver passes the component id
the factory was registered under, so a view such as `rect()` knows which component holds its pose; a bare
function resolver passes no id.
entries.signature: type EntityViewFactory = (row: RenderRow, componentId?: string) => EntityView | undefined;

entries.name: EntityViewResolver
entries.doc:
Which view an entity gets: one factory for every entity, or factories by component id (the first id, in the
record's own key order, whose component the entity has wins).
entries.signature: type EntityViewResolver = EntityViewFactory | Readonly<Record<string, EntityViewFactory>>;

entries.name: FILTER_VERTEX
entries.doc:
The GLSL vertex stage every AF filter shares: it passes the texture coordinate and the pixel position
(`vPixelCoord`) to the fragment stage.

entries.name: filterPrograms
entries.doc:
Builds a filter's programs from its GLSL and WGSL fragment stages on the shared vertex stages, so WebGL2
stays at parity with WebGPU (AGENTS.md).
entries.signature: function filterPrograms(name: string, fragmentGlsl: string, fragmentWgsl: string): FilterProgramsResult;

entries.name: FilterProgramsResult
entries.doc: A filter's WebGL2 and WebGPU programs, for a Pixi `Filter`'s `glProgram` and `gpuProgram`.

entries.name: interpolatePose
entries.doc:
The pose between the previous tick (`alpha = 0`) and the current one (`alpha = 1`). With no previous tick
(just added, or after a resync) it is the current pose. A missing `angle`, or a non-numeric `x`/`y`, is 0.
entries.signature: function interpolatePose(curr: Readonly<FieldRecord>, prev: Readonly<FieldRecord> | undefined, alpha: number): Pose;

entries.name: lerp
entries.doc: Linear blend; `t = 1` returns `b` exactly, because `a + (b - a)` can round away from it.
entries.signature: function lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number;

entries.name: lerpAngle
entries.doc:
Blends two angles (radians) along the shorter arc, so a body turning from just under π to just over -π
swings through π instead of spinning the long way round through 0. At `t = 1` it returns `b` exactly, so a
view at rest shows the sim's own value rather than an equivalent angle 2π away.
entries.signature: function lerpAngle(a: number, b: number, t: number): number;

entries.name: LetterboxFrame
entries.doc:
The containers a letterboxed scene is built from (backdrop, world, ui, mask and bars), laid out for a view
size by `layout`.

entries.name: LetterboxGeometry
entries.doc:
Where `LetterboxFrame.layout` put the playfield in the view, in screen px: its scale and rect, the gameplay
and scenery areas, and whether the view is portrait.

entries.name: LetterboxOptions
entries.doc:
A letterbox's logical playfield size and its bar and field colours (defaults `DEFAULT_BAR_FRACTION`,
`DEFAULT_BAR_COLOR`, `DEFAULT_FIELD_COLOR`).

entries.name: MAX_RESOLUTION
entries.doc: The highest canvas resolution (device pixels per CSS pixel) the renderer uses, at the `high` quality tier.
entries.signature: const MAX_RESOLUTION = 2;

entries.name: meetsTier
entries.doc: Whether `tier` is `min` or higher: a pass registered for `medium` runs at `medium` and `high`.
entries.signature: function meetsTier(tier: QualityTier, min: QualityTier): boolean;

entries.name: PixiRenderer
entries.doc: The runtime's `GameRenderer`, built on PixiJS, with its stage.

entries.name: PixiRendererOptions
entries.doc: Options for `createPixiRenderer`; every field has a default.

entries.name: PixiStage
entries.doc:
The Pixi scene the renderer draws, as a game's `setup` sees it: the app, the letterbox's layers, the entity
views, the post-filter slot and the quality tier.

entries.name: PixiStageHooks
entries.doc: What a `setup` may return to hear every step, frame and reset (DX spec §3.4, DX.3 decision E-1).

entries.name: PORTRAIT_FIELD_TOP
entries.doc:
The most room above the playfield in a portrait view, in screen px (the HUD's top margin, M1 render-pixi spec):
the field sits this far down, or centred when centring leaves less room above it.
entries.signature: const PORTRAIT_FIELD_TOP = 60;

entries.name: portraitFieldHeight
entries.doc:
The playfield's logical height in a portrait view: what fits below `PORTRAIT_FIELD_TOP` and above the
`band` of on-screen controls at `scale`, and never less than `baseHeight`.
entries.signature: function portraitFieldHeight(viewHeight: number, scale: number, band: number, baseHeight?: number): number;

entries.name: Pose
entries.doc: Where an entity view draws: position in world pixels and rotation in radians (Pixi `rotation`).

entries.name: poseComponent
entries.doc:
The component a view reads its pose from: the one it was registered under, or (for a bare function
resolver, which has no id) the first component in row order with numeric `x` and `y`.
entries.signature: function poseComponent(components: Components, componentId?: string | undefined): Readonly<FieldRecord> | undefined;

entries.name: postFilter
entries.doc:
Declares a screen-space filter over the whole picture: `renderer: { postFilters: [postFilter('vignette', {
glsl, wgsl })] }`. The renderer builds it when it starts and keeps it in the stage's post-filter slot under
`name`. A filter that cannot be built, or whose GLSL does not link, is left out with a warning and the frame
draws without it. Throws when the name or either shader is empty.
entries.signature: function postFilter(name: string, spec: PostFilterSpec): PostFilterDef;

entries.name: PostFilterDef
entries.doc: A declared filter, as `postFilter` returns it and `PixiRendererOptions.postFilters` takes it.

entries.name: PostFilterOptions
entries.doc: Options for `PostFilterSlot.set`.

entries.name: PostFilterSlot
entries.doc:
The post-filter slot (PRODUCT spec §2 F1): each owner (an extension, quality tiers, the game) keeps its own
filters under its id, and the slot writes all of them to the target, ordered by `order` (lower first), then
by id. Once a slot is in use it owns the target's `filters`; assigning them directly is overwritten on the
next change. Filters stay GLSL + WGSL pairs (`filterPrograms`), so WebGL2 keeps parity with WebGPU.

Quality tiers (M4 spec §4.11): an owner may declare the lowest tier it runs at. Below it, its filters are left
out of the composed list but kept, so raising the tier brings them back in their place. An owner without a
`minTier` (the art direction, such as a palette lock) runs at every tier.

entries.name: PostFilterSpec
entries.doc:
What a screen-space filter is made of: the same effect written twice, for WebGL2 (`glsl`) and WebGPU (`wgsl`),
so the two renderers stay at parity. Both are fragment shaders that `filterPrograms` joins to the shared vertex
stage: GLSL reads `vTextureCoord`, `vPixelCoord` and `uTexture`; WGSL has `mainFragment(input: VSOutput)`.

entries.name: PostFilterTarget
entries.doc: Where the composed filters go: `PixiStage` (its scene's `filters`), or any Pixi container.

entries.name: QualityBuild
entries.doc: What `rebuildOnQuality` keeps mounted.

entries.name: rebuildOnQuality
entries.doc:
Keeps something built for the player's quality tier (M4 spec §4.11), rebuilding it when the tier changes.

Quality decides which passes a build makes at all, so a change is a rebuild, not a toggle. The old build is
destroyed before the new one is made: two live builds would both hold their GPU resources. From FloorFifty
`apps/client/src/systems/render/quality-rebuild.ts` at `ac72660`, over runtime's `SettingsStore` with `read`
picking the tier out of the game's settings.

entries.name: rect
entries.doc:
A filled rectangle that follows its component's `x`, `y` and `angle`, interpolated between ticks:
`entityViews: { [Body.id]: rect({ w: 8, h: 8, color: 0xf9c22b }) }`.
entries.signature: function rect(options: RectViewOptions): EntityViewFactory;

entries.name: RectViewOptions
entries.doc: A `rect` view's size, colour and anchor.

entries.name: RenderDeltaConsumer
entries.doc:
Keeps one entity view per sim entity in the world container from each step's render delta, and interpolates
them between ticks.

entries.name: RendererPreference
entries.doc: The renderer backend: `webgl` (WebGL2, the default) or `webgpu` (opt-in).
entries.signature: type RendererPreference = "webgl" | "webgpu";

entries.name: RESOLUTION_CAPS
entries.doc: The canvas resolution each quality tier allows at most (M4 spec §4.11).
entries.signature: const RESOLUTION_CAPS: Readonly<Record<QualityTier, number>>;

entries.name: SHAKE_DECAY
entries.doc: Trauma lost per second: a full shake (1) is gone in 2/3 s.
entries.signature: const SHAKE_DECAY = 1.5;

entries.name: SHAKE_MAX_OFFSET
entries.doc: The largest shake offset per axis, in logical px, at trauma 1.
entries.signature: const SHAKE_MAX_OFFSET = 8;

entries.name: sprite
entries.doc:
A sprite that follows its component's `x`, `y` and `angle`, interpolated between ticks. `source` is a
texture or a url: a url the runtime already loaded (it is in `Assets.cache`) shows at once; otherwise the
sprite is empty until `Assets.load` resolves. A url that fails to load is reported with `reportError`
and the sprite stays empty. The frame textures are sliced once per factory and shared by its sprites.
With `frame`, the url is an atlas page's Spritesheet and the sprite shows that frame; a name the atlas lacks
is reported the same way.
entries.signature: function sprite(source: Texture | string, options?: SpriteViewOptions): EntityViewFactory;

entries.name: SpriteFrames
entries.doc:
The texture is a sheet of equal frames, read left to right, top to bottom. The pose component's numeric
`frame` field picks one (floored, wrapped by the frame count); with no `frame` field the first is shown.
Frames switch on ticks; they are not interpolated.

entries.name: SpriteViewOptions
entries.doc: A `sprite` view's anchor and either its sprite-sheet frames or one frame of a packed atlas.

entries.name: ViewAnchor
entries.doc: Where the view's own box sits on its position: 0 = left/top, 0.5 = centre, 1 = right/bottom.

entries.name: WGSL_FILTER_HEADER
entries.doc:
The WGSL counterpart of `FILTER_VERTEX`: the filter uniforms and bindings and the vertex stage, which
passes the pixel position to the fragment stage.

entries.name: actionsForGesture
entries.doc: Every action `gesture` drives in `profile` (M4.3); none when it is unbound.
entries.signature: function actionsForGesture(profile: InputProfile, gesture: GestureName): string[];

entries.name: actionsForKey
entries.doc: Every action `code` (a `KeyboardEvent.code`) drives in `profile`; none when it is unbound.
entries.signature: function actionsForKey(profile: InputProfile, code: string): string[];

entries.name: actionsForPadButton
entries.doc: Every action the standard-mapping pad button `index` drives in `profile`; none when it is unbound.
entries.signature: function actionsForPadButton(profile: InputProfile, index: number): string[];

entries.name: ActiveDevice
entries.doc: The device of the last real input, and the button labels of the active pad (`generic` before any pad).

entries.name: AppLoop
entries.doc:
The frame loop service: `run` steps a sim at its fixed tick rate from display frames, with the commands for each
tick, and the renderer draws every frame. No step runs while `Time` is paused; a throw from a step stops it.

entries.name: applyDocumentLocale
entries.doc: `<html lang dir>`: the browser picks glyph forms and line breaking from `lang`, and the layout direction from `dir`.
entries.signature: function applyDocumentLocale(element: HTMLElement, locale: string): void;

entries.name: applyOverrides
entries.doc:
The game's profile with the player's overrides applied (M4 spec §6): an override for an unknown action, one that
binds a reserved input, or one with a pad button out of range is dropped and named in `dropped` (sorted), and the
defaults stand for it. Overrides saved against another profile are all dropped.

entries.name: AssetLoadFailed
entries.doc: An asset download failed with a non-OK HTTP status or network error (status 0).
entries.signature: class AssetLoadFailed extends AssetLoadFailedBase {}

entries.name: Assets
entries.doc:
The asset loader service: `load` fetches a screen's assets and fonts with progress, failing
`AssetLoadFailed` or `LoadStalled`; `get` returns a loaded file by path.

entries.name: Audio
entries.doc:
The audio service (M5 spec §4.6): one-shot sounds and looping music on the audio buses, unlocked by the
first gesture after `session.ready`; the game runs silent when no audio context can be built.

entries.name: AUDIO_BUS_NAMES
entries.doc:
The core audio buses (PRODUCT spec §2 F1): `master` carries the other four; M5-D3 added `voice` (announcers,
dialogue). Every change to the set is an API change (PRODUCT spec §2 F6).
entries.signature: const AUDIO_BUS_NAMES: readonly ["master", "music", "sfx", "ui", "voice"];

entries.name: AUDIO_SETTINGS_DEFAULT
entries.doc: Not muted, every bus at full.
entries.signature: const AUDIO_SETTINGS_DEFAULT: AudioSettings;

entries.name: AudioBuses
entries.doc:
The audio-bus seam (PRODUCT spec §2 F1). M5's core audio implements it over Web Audio (a gain node per bus
into `master`, combined there with `Hosting.audio`'s volume and focus); an extension such as Plus
`audio-stream`, or the game, connects its sources to `input(bus)` and never to the destination directly,
so the player's gains and the host's ducking always apply.
The `AudioBuses` service tag. Core provides no implementation until M5.

entries.name: AudioBusGains
entries.doc: The player's gain per bus, 0 (silent) to 1 (full), as a game's settings store it.
entries.signature: type AudioBusGains = Readonly<Record<AudioBusName, number>>;

entries.name: audioBusGainsSchema
entries.doc:
Validates saved bus gains; a bus left out is at full gain. A gain outside 0..1 fails the parse rather than
being clamped, so `SettingsDef`'s fallback to defaults (runtime `readSettings`) applies to a bad record.
entries.signature: const audioBusGainsSchema: z.ZodType<AudioBusGains, Partial<Record<AudioBusName, number | undefined>>>;

entries.name: AudioBusName
entries.doc: One of `AUDIO_BUS_NAMES`.
entries.signature: type AudioBusName = (typeof AUDIO_BUS_NAMES)[number];

entries.name: AudioContextLike
entries.doc: The part of `AudioContext` the graph uses. `interrupted` is Safari's state for a call or Siri.

entries.name: AudioDecodeFailed
entries.doc:
The browser could not decode a sound's bytes (M5 spec §6): that sound is silent and nothing else stops. The
`audio.decode.failed` fact carries the same alias.
entries.signature: class AudioDecodeFailed extends AudioDecodeFailedBase {}

entries.name: AudioDecodeFailedFields
entries.doc: The fields of `AudioDecodeFailed`.

entries.name: audioLayer
entries.doc: `makeAudio` with its defaults, reading `Hosting`, `Assets` and `PresentationBus` from the runtime.
entries.signature: const audioLayer: (options?: AudioOptions) => Layer.Layer<Audio | AudioBuses, never, Hosting | Assets | PresentationBus>;

entries.name: AudioLive
entries.doc: The Audio service with its defaults: the browser's `AudioContext`, `window`, `document` and `fetch`.
entries.signature: const AudioLive: Layer.Layer<Audio | AudioBuses, never, Hosting | Assets | PresentationBus>;

entries.name: AudioOptions
entries.doc: Options for the audio service; each has a browser default, replaced in tests.

entries.name: AudioServices
entries.doc: What the service reads from the runtime.

entries.name: AudioSettings
entries.doc:
The player's audio choices (M5 spec §7, M5.4), as FloorFifty's `audio` settings: the mute, the mute while another
window has focus, and a gain per bus. The one owner of their shape: the Settings screen's Audio group and the
`Audio` service read it from here. Kept on the device, not in the player's saves (§4.5): `CORE_SETTINGS.deviceFields`.

entries.name: audioSettingsSchema
entries.doc: A missing field takes its default; a bad record reads as the defaults, as every settings field falls back.
entries.signature: const audioSettingsSchema: z.ZodType<AudioSettings, unknown>;

entries.name: AuthoritativeSnapshot
entries.doc:
One authoritative state: the authority sim's `snapshot()` bytes at `tick`, with its `hash()`. A receiver
`restore`s the bytes and may compare its own hash to `hash` to detect divergence.

entries.name: AutosavePolicy
entries.doc:
When the loaded slot writes itself: on each listed trigger, with `intervalSeconds` for the `interval`
timer.

entries.name: AutosaveTrigger
entries.doc: What can make the loaded slot write itself (M5 spec §4.4).
entries.signature: type AutosaveTrigger = "screen-exit" | "round-end" | "background" | "interval";

entries.name: BindingOverride
entries.doc: What the player changed about one action: its keys, its pad buttons, or both.

entries.name: BoardEntry
entries.doc: One row of a board, as Ruken gives it; `isMe` marks the player.
entries.signature: type BoardEntry = Effect.Effect.Success<ReturnType<HostingLeaderboards["get"]>>["entries"][number];

entries.name: BoardQuery
entries.doc: What `readBoard` asks for: Ruken's `get` options (`scope` `top` or `around-me`, `limit`).
entries.signature: type BoardQuery = NonNullable<Parameters<HostingLeaderboards["get"]>[1]>;

entries.name: BoardState
entries.doc: The state of a board after the game's last submit to it.

entries.name: BoardView
entries.doc: A board read for a screen: its rows, or why there are none.

entries.name: BootDefect
entries.doc: An unexpected defect during boot.
entries.signature: class BootDefect extends BootDefectBase {}

entries.name: BootError
entries.doc: Every way boot can fail; each draws on the runtime's boot failure panel (shared contracts §4).
entries.signature: type BootError = HostError | ContentHashMismatch | AssetLoadFailed | LoadStalled | RendererUnavailable | BootDefect;

entries.name: browserHaptics
entries.doc: The browser's haptics: its pads, its `vibrate`, and whether its pointer is a finger.
entries.signature: function browserHaptics(target: Window): Haptics;

entries.name: CAMERA_SETTINGS_DEFAULT
entries.doc: The camera choices a new player starts with: the default turn speed, not inverted.
entries.signature: const CAMERA_SETTINGS_DEFAULT: CameraSettings;

entries.name: CAMERA_TURN_SPEED
entries.doc:
The range of "Camera turn speed" in degrees per dragged pixel (M4 spec §16.3.6, M3 spec §4.2): 0.25° by default,
so a 1,440 px sweep is one full turn. A Settings slider steps through it.

entries.name: CameraDragTracker
entries.doc:
Turns pointer samples into camera drags for one `DragSink`: one pointer at a time, its horizontal CSS px per move,
from a touch or pen's primary contact or the mouse's secondary button.

entries.name: CameraSettings
entries.doc:
The player's camera choices, `camera` in the core settings: how far a dragged pixel turns the camera, and whether
the turn is inverted. The one owner of their shape: the game's Settings rows (GAME-3D) and its command mapping
(`turnUnitsFromPixels`) read them from here.

entries.name: cameraSettingsSchema
entries.doc:
A missing, malformed or out-of-range field reads as its default, keeping the other; a record that is not an
object reads as the defaults, as every settings field falls back.
entries.signature: const cameraSettingsSchema: z.ZodType<CameraSettings, unknown>;

entries.name: Capture
entries.doc: The input a capture caught: a key by its `KeyboardEvent.code`, or a standard-mapping pad button.

entries.name: CompiledContentData
entries.doc: The compiled JSON content read by the runtime (spec §3.3).

entries.name: ContentHashMismatch
entries.doc: Content hash does not match expected hash.
entries.signature: class ContentHashMismatch extends ContentHashMismatchBase {}

entries.name: contentHashOf
entries.signature: function contentHashOf(data: unknown): string;

entries.name: CORE_SETTINGS
entries.doc:
The `settings` save, version 1: the player's bindings (`input`), graphics quality (`display`), audio (`audio`),
vibration (`haptics`) and camera turn (`camera`).
entries.signature: const CORE_SETTINGS: SettingsDef<CoreSettings>;

entries.name: CoreSettings
entries.doc: The settings every game carries: input bindings, display, audio and vibration.

entries.name: createHaptics
entries.doc: The haptics service over these sources; it starts enabled.
entries.signature: function createHaptics(options: HapticsOptions): Haptics;

entries.name: createT
entries.doc:
`t` over a messages module (`import * as m from './paraglide/messages.js'`). Each call reads the current
locale, so a screen that calls `t` again after `'locale.changed'` shows the new language without a remount.
An unknown key throws, naming it: the types already forbid it, so it means the catalog and the code drifted.
entries.signature: function createT<Messages extends Record<string, unknown>>(messages: Messages): Translate<Messages>;

entries.name: DEFAULT_QUALITY
entries.doc: `high` until PRODUCT.7 has measured the phone profiles (M4-D6); no device auto-detection.
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_QUALITY: QualityTier;

entries.name: defineSave
entries.doc: Declares a save. It checks nothing the SDK checks; it only gives the definition its type.
entries.signature: function defineSave<S>(def: SaveDef<S>): SaveDef<S>;

entries.name: DeviceStorage
entries.doc:
Where a settings field that belongs to one device is kept (M5 spec §4.5, M5-D4). Any method may throw, as a
blocked or full `localStorage` does; the settings store copes with that and never falls back to the saves.

entries.name: DisplayCopy
entries.doc:
The words of the display policy: the landscape gate, the rotate hint for each orientation and the rotate
toast.

entries.name: DisplaySettings
entries.doc: The core display settings a game's settings carry as `display`: `{ display: displaySettingsSchema }`.

entries.name: displaySettingsSchema
entries.doc: The schema of `DisplaySettings`: an unknown or missing quality reads as `DEFAULT_QUALITY`.

entries.name: DragPointer
entries.doc: What drove a drag: a finger or pen (`touch`), or the mouse.
entries.signature: type DragPointer = "touch" | "mouse";

entries.name: DragSink
entries.doc: Where drags go (`Input.drag`): CSS px moved to the right since the previous move, negative to the left.

entries.name: DragStart
entries.doc: The parts of a `pointerdown` that decide whether it may drag.

entries.name: EventScores
entries.doc: A sim event's type (its `defineEvent` id) → the board it scores on and the score its payload gives.

entries.name: EventSounds
entries.doc: A sim event's type (its `defineEvent` id) → the asset path it plays, or the path with its bus and gain.

entries.name: Flow
entries.doc:
The screen flow service: the current screen, `dispatch` to follow an event's transition from it, `openMenu`
for the current screen's menu, and `settled` once no transition is pending.

entries.name: FlowFailure
entries.doc: Why entering a screen failed: an asset load, a stalled download, or the screen's own failure.

entries.name: formatDateTime
entries.doc:
A moment as a date and a short time in the reader's convention, in the reader's zone unless `options.timeZone`
names one (a test names UTC). A save's time on the slot list is this.
entries.signature: const formatDateTime: (locale: string, epochMs: number, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) => string;

entries.name: formatDuration
entries.doc:
A clock-style duration from milliseconds, whole seconds: `01:15`, or `1:02:05` once there are hours.
Each part is a locale number (Arabic-Indic digits in `ar-EG`); the separator is a colon. NumberFormat, not
Intl.DurationFormat, so it needs no ES2025 lib in a game's tsconfig and runs on engines without it.
entries.signature: function formatDuration(locale: string, milliseconds: number): string;

entries.name: formatNumber
entries.doc: A number in `locale`'s convention (Intl.NumberFormat with `options`).
entries.signature: const formatNumber: (locale: string, value: number, options?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions) => string;

entries.name: formatPercent
entries.doc: A whole percentage of a fraction: 0.5 → `50%` (`50 %` in French).
entries.signature: const formatPercent: (locale: string, fraction: number) => string;

entries.name: FrameInfo
entries.doc:
One display frame: the interpolation alpha between the last two ticks, the frame's length in ms, and
whether time is paused.

entries.name: GameDefinition
entries.doc: Everything a game provides to the runtime to boot (spec §3.3).

entries.name: GameOrientation
entries.doc: The orientation a game plays in; the ship config writes the same value as `runtime.orientation`.
entries.signature: type GameOrientation = "portrait" | "landscape" | "any";

entries.name: GameRenderer
entries.doc: What the runtime asks of a renderer: apply each step's result, draw each frame, and reset for a new sim.

entries.name: GESTURE_TUNING
entries.doc: FloorFifty's gesture tuning, the defaults.
entries.signature: const GESTURE_TUNING: GestureTuning;

entries.name: GestureName
entries.doc: A touch gesture (M4.3 recognises the swipes, flick and tap; M4.12 the camera drag).
entries.signature: type GestureName = (typeof GESTURE_NAMES)[number];

entries.name: GestureSink
entries.doc:
Where gestures go: held while a finger steers, pulsed for a flick or a tap. The camera drag is analog (M4.12) and
goes to `Input.drag` instead, so it is not one of these.

entries.name: GestureTuning
entries.doc: Content tuning, in CSS px and ms; FloorFifty's values are the defaults.

entries.name: GlyphFamily
entries.doc: Which labels a pad's buttons carry, read from its id.
entries.signature: type GlyphFamily = "xbox" | "playstation" | "generic";

entries.name: HapticPulse
entries.doc: One pulse: a pad's dual-rumble (milliseconds, each motor 0..1), and a phone's buzz in `navigator.vibrate`'s terms.

entries.name: Haptics
entries.doc:
The haptics service: a pad's rumble or a phone's buzz, when the device can and the player's Vibration
setting allows.

entries.name: HapticsOptions
entries.doc:
Where the haptics service finds pads, the vibrate call and whether this is a touch screen; replaced in
tests.

entries.name: HapticsSettings
entries.doc: The player's Vibration setting: whether `Haptics` pulses at all.

entries.name: hapticsSettingsSchema
entries.doc: On unless saved off; a bad record reads as on, as every settings field falls back.
entries.signature: const hapticsSettingsSchema: z.ZodType<HapticsSettings, unknown>;

entries.name: Input
entries.doc:
The input service (M4 spec §4.2): held actions from keys, pads, touch buttons and gestures under the game's
profile and the player's overrides, menu edges, the active device and pads, and rebinding.

entries.name: INPUT_SETTINGS_DEFAULT
entries.doc: Nothing changed: the game's profile as it ships.
entries.signature: const INPUT_SETTINGS_DEFAULT: InputSettings;

entries.name: InputBinding
entries.doc: What drives one action: keys by `KeyboardEvent.code` (layout independent), pad buttons, an on-screen button.

entries.name: InputContext
entries.doc: Where an action is live: during play, in menus, or both.
entries.signature: type InputContext = "play" | "menu" | "any";

entries.name: InputContextNow
entries.doc: What input drives now: `play` (the game's bindings) or `menu` (the menu actions).
entries.signature: type InputContextNow = "play" | "menu";

entries.name: InputDevice
entries.doc: A kind of input device.
entries.signature: type InputDevice = "keyboard" | "gamepad" | "touch";

entries.name: InputOptions
entries.doc:
What the input service listens to: the window, the game's profile, the bus, and optionally the settings and
the host's input mode.

entries.name: InputProfile
entries.doc:
A named set of bindings, one per game action (PRODUCT spec §2 F1). It is data: a settings screen rebinds a
copy and saves it in the game's `SettingsDef`; M4's input service reads it. Action ids are the game's own.

entries.name: InputProfileInput
entries.doc: What `inputProfileSchema` accepts: every binding field may be left out.

entries.name: inputProfileSchema
entries.doc:
Validates an input profile, filling left-out binding fields with "unbound". A reserved key or pad button fails
the parse with the action named (M4-D3, I-j): at boot that is a developer error before anything renders.
