entries.signature: const inputProfileSchema: z.ZodType<InputProfile, InputProfileInput>;

entries.name: InputSettings
entries.doc:
The player's input settings, kept in the game's settings as `input`: the profile, the per-action overrides
and the touch mode.

entries.name: inputSettingsSchema
entries.doc:
The `input` field of a game's settings schema: `{ input: inputSettingsSchema }`. A record that does not read is
the default, as every settings field falls back (`readSettings`); a single bad override is `applyOverrides`'s to
drop, so the player's other bindings survive it.
entries.signature: const inputSettingsSchema: z.ZodType<InputSettings, unknown>;

entries.name: Leaderboards
entries.doc: `Board` is the game's board ids (its ship config's `leaderboards` keys); `string` until a game narrows it.

entries.name: liveDeviceStorage
entries.doc:
The game frame's own `localStorage` as a device, with `prefix:` before every key so two games on one origin do
not meet. Undefined where merely reaching `window.localStorage` throws (blocked site data, a sandbox): the
settings store then holds device fields for the visit only.

This is the declared stand-in for a host-owned device scope (Ruken request R-6), and a choice per settings field,
not a fallback for a denied `saves` grant.
entries.signature: function liveDeviceStorage(win: Pick<Window, "localStorage">, prefix: string): DeviceStorage | undefined;

entries.name: Loaded
entries.doc: A slot loaded for play.

entries.name: LoadMeter
entries.doc:
Watches downloads: `guard` fails a wait with `LoadStalled` after `STALL_MS` without progress, and calls its
`onSlow` after `SLOW_MS`.

entries.name: LoadStalled
entries.doc:
A resource download had no progress reported for STALL_MS (30 s).
Triggers the "Taking a while" screen with a Try again button.
entries.signature: class LoadStalled extends LoadStalledBase {}

entries.name: Locale
entries.doc:
The locale service (PRODUCT spec §4): the game's locales, the one text is drawn in now, the player's choice
and the text direction.

entries.name: LOCALE_SAVE_KEY
entries.doc: The save key of the player's language choice; absent means Automatic (negotiated).
entries.signature: const LOCALE_SAVE_KEY = "automata.locale";

entries.name: LocaleCandidates
entries.doc: The candidates, best first; each is used only when the game has a matching locale.

entries.name: LocaleDef
entries.doc:
The game's languages. A Paraglide-generated `runtime.js` satisfies it as is
(`import * as runtime from './paraglide/runtime.js'`), and then its messages answer in this locale.

entries.name: makeAudio
entries.doc:
Builds the Audio service, which is also the `AudioBuses` seam. Nothing is built until the first gesture after
the session is ready; closing the scope stops every sound, closes the context and removes every listener.
entries.signature: const makeAudio: (options: AudioServices & AudioOptions) => Effect.Effect<Audio & AudioBuses, never, Scope.Scope>;

entries.name: makeInput
entries.doc: Builds the Input over `target` for the scope's life: closing the scope removes every listener.
entries.signature: function makeInput(options: InputOptions): Effect.Effect<Input, never, Scope.Scope>;

entries.name: makeLeaderboards
entries.doc:
Builds the leaderboards service over `Hosting`; each submit's state is published as
`leaderboard.submitted`.
entries.signature: const makeLeaderboards: Effect.Effect<Leaderboards, never, Hosting | PresentationBus>;

entries.name: makeSaves
entries.doc:
Opens the game's save for boot, with its triggers and its exit flush, for as long as the scope is open. A game
without `saves` gets a `Saves` that holds nothing, and nothing is read from the host.

entries.name: matchLocale
entries.doc:
The game's locale for a requested tag: the same tag (ignoring case), else the first locale with the same
primary language subtag. `fr-CA` finds `fr`; `pt` finds `pt-BR`. Undefined when the game lacks the language.
entries.signature: function matchLocale(requested: string, locales: readonly string[]): string | undefined;

entries.name: MAX_FRAME_MS
entries.doc: The Last Light clock.ts 0.1 s clamp: at most 6 steps at 60 Hz, the rest is dropped
entries.signature: const MAX_FRAME_MS = 100;

entries.name: MAX_TURN_UNITS_PER_STEP
entries.doc: The most one step's `camera-turn` may carry either way: 45°.
entries.signature: const MAX_TURN_UNITS_PER_STEP = 8192;

entries.name: MenuAction
entries.doc: A fixed menu action: it drives menus and the pause screen, never the sim.
entries.signature: type MenuAction = "nav-up" | "nav-down" | "nav-left" | "nav-right" | "confirm" | "back" | "page-prev" | "page-next" | "adjust-dec" | "adjust-inc" | "pause";

entries.name: MessageFunction
entries.doc: One compiled message: Paraglide passes its inputs as one object.
entries.signature: type MessageFunction = (inputs?: any) => string;

entries.name: MusicOptions
entries.doc: Options for `Audio.music`: where to begin and which region loops.

entries.name: negotiateLocale
entries.doc:
The order is the player's saved choice, Ruken's session locale, the browser's languages, the default
(PRODUCT spec §4 item 2, as decided 2026-10-16: a choice made in the game's own picker outranks the
platform's, as in FloorFifty, where detection runs only "when the player has not chosen one").
Each step that names a language the game lacks falls through to the next.
entries.signature: function negotiateLocale(candidates: LocaleCandidates): string;

entries.name: NetworkPort
entries.doc:
The networking seam (PRODUCT spec §2 F1): remote commands in, authoritative snapshots out. The sim already
takes `Command`s and restores snapshot bytes, so the port carries exactly those; the wire format, rooms,
prediction and reconciliation belong to whatever implements it (Plus `net`, M7) or to the game.

An authority listens with `onRemoteCommand` and answers with `publishSnapshot`; a client sends with
`sendCommand` and listens with `onSnapshot`. One implementation may serve either role.

Commands cross the port every tick, so its members are plain callbacks rather than Effects (ADR 0003: no
Effect allocation per frame). Sends never throw: a transport failure is the implementation's to report
(for example as a presentation-bus fact), never a silent switch to another path. Each `on*` returns its
unsubscribe; a listener removed, or registered after the port's scope closed, receives nothing.
The `NetworkPort` service tag. Core provides no implementation; an extension or the game provides one.

entries.name: PadInfo
entries.doc: A connected pad. Only `standard` pads drive bindings (DX spec §3.3).

entries.name: ParaglideRuntime
entries.doc: The parts of a Paraglide-generated `runtime.js` the runtime uses. Method syntax, so a narrower `Locale` union fits.

entries.name: PauseReason
entries.doc:
`input`: the active pad was unplugged during play (M4-D9); Resume on the pause screen clears it. `display`: a phone
is held the other way from the game's orientation (M4.7); turning it back clears it.
entries.signature: type PauseReason = "lifecycle" | "menu" | "input" | "display";

entries.name: pluralCategory
entries.doc: The CLDR plural (or, with 'ordinal', ordinal) category of a count: one, two, few, many, zero or other.
entries.signature: const pluralCategory: (locale: string, count: number, type?: Intl.PluralRuleType) => Intl.LDMLPluralRule;

entries.name: PresentationBus
entries.doc:
The presentation bus: typed facts the runtime publishes for screens, audio and tests to hear. Facts
describe what happened; they never change gameplay state.

entries.name: QUALITY_TIERS
entries.doc:
Graphics quality (M4 spec §4.11). A lower tier caps the canvas resolution and leaves out the post-filter owners
registered for a higher one; it never drops the art direction. The one owner of the tier: render-pixi and the
Settings screen's Display section read it from here.
entries.signature: const QUALITY_TIERS: readonly ["high", "medium", "low"];

entries.name: QualityTier
entries.doc: A graphics quality tier: `high`, `medium` or `low`.
entries.signature: type QualityTier = (typeof QUALITY_TIERS)[number];

entries.name: qualityTierSchema
entries.doc: A tier; an unknown saved value reads as the default, as every settings field falls back.
entries.signature: const qualityTierSchema: z.ZodType<QualityTier, unknown>;

entries.name: REBIND_TIMEOUT_MS
entries.doc: How long `capture` waits for a press (M4 spec §4.2, §6).
entries.signature: const REBIND_TIMEOUT_MS = 1e4;

entries.name: RebindCancelled
entries.doc: The player pressed Escape or pad B while a capture waited: nothing changes.
entries.signature: class RebindCancelled extends RebindCancelledBase {}

entries.name: RebindConflict
entries.doc: Refused: the input would leave `with`, a required action, with nothing on that device (M4-D4).
entries.signature: class RebindConflict extends RebindConflictBase {}

entries.name: RebindError
entries.doc: Why a rebind was refused, with nothing changed.
entries.signature: type RebindError = RebindConflict | RebindReserved | RebindUnknown;

entries.name: rebindProfile
entries.doc:
Binds `capture` to `action` on `device` (M4 spec §4.5, M4-D4): it becomes the action's only input there and
leaves every other action live in an overlapping context. Refused, with nothing changed, when the input is
reserved or when it would leave a `required` action with nothing on that device. The result is the overrides
over `defaults` for the whole profile, ready to save.
entries.signature: function rebindProfile(defaults: InputProfile, current: InputProfile, action: string, device: "keyboard" | "gamepad", capture: Capture): Either.Either<Record<string, BindingOverride>, RebindError>;

entries.name: RebindReserved
entries.doc: Refused: Escape, Tab, pad 8 or pad 16 (M4-D3), or a pad button the standard mapping does not have.
entries.signature: class RebindReserved extends RebindReservedBase {}

entries.name: RebindTimedOut
entries.doc: Nothing was pressed for `REBIND_TIMEOUT_MS`: nothing changes.
entries.signature: class RebindTimedOut extends RebindTimedOutBase {}

entries.name: RebindUnknown
entries.doc: Refused: the profile has no such action.
entries.signature: class RebindUnknown extends RebindUnknownBase {}

entries.name: Renderer
entries.doc: The game's renderer as a runtime service.
entries.signature: const Renderer: Context.Tag<GameRenderer, GameRenderer>;

entries.name: RendererFactory
entries.doc:
Builds the game's renderer on a render target in a scope, failing `RendererUnavailable` when it cannot
start.
entries.signature: type RendererFactory = (target: RenderTarget) => Effect.Effect<GameRenderer, RendererUnavailable, Scope.Scope>;

entries.name: RendererUnavailable
entries.doc:
Neither WebGL2 nor WebGPU could be initialized.
In Ruken this presents the "unsupported" screen with an exit button.
entries.signature: class RendererUnavailable extends RendererUnavailableBase {}

entries.name: RenderTarget
entries.doc: Where a renderer draws: the host element, the layout geometry, the loaded assets and the presentation bus.

entries.name: RESERVED_KEYS
entries.doc: Keys never bindable in a game's profile: Escape (the one back path) and Tab (focus).
entries.signature: const RESERVED_KEYS: readonly string[];

entries.name: RESERVED_PAD_BUTTONS
entries.doc:
Never bindable in a game's profile (M4-D3): Ruken's SDK summons the host on pad 8 (View), 16 is Home, Escape is the
one back path and Tab moves focus.
entries.signature: const RESERVED_PAD_BUTTONS: readonly number[];

entries.name: RotateHintMode
entries.doc: How a game locked to one orientation says so (Owner amendment, 2026-10-18): a blocking cover, or a toast.
entries.signature: type RotateHintMode = "block" | "toast";

entries.name: runGame
entries.doc:
Boots and runs the game in a runtime Scope (spec §4 Failure and Shutdown).

Each attempt runs in a fresh Scope. On failure, mounts BootFailurePanel and keeps
the attempt scope open so Back to {host} can access its Hosting service. Try again
and Continue without loading close the failed attempt scope and re-run bootProgram
in a fresh Scope on the same root without reloading the page.

RuntimeHandle.shutdown() closes the runtime scope, running all finalizers in LIFO order.
entries.signature: function runGame<S>(game: GameDefinition<S>): RuntimeHandle;

entries.name: RuntimeFacts
entries.doc: Every fact the runtime publishes on the presentation bus, by name.

entries.name: RuntimeHandle
entries.doc: Controls the running game: shutdown closes the runtime scope (spec §3.3, planning note 11).

entries.name: RuntimeSeams
entries.doc: Test seams injected into the runtime boot program (spec §3.3, planning note 10).

entries.name: RuntimeServices
entries.doc: The runtime services a screen's `enter` may use.
entries.signature: type RuntimeServices = Hosting | PresentationBus | Time | Flow | Settings | Saves | AppLoop | Assets | GameRenderer | Locale | Audio | AudioBuses | Leaderboards | Haptics;

entries.name: Save
entries.doc:
A game's save (M5 spec §4.3): its slots' states, load, write and remove, and the progress `touch` keeps for
the autosave triggers to write.

entries.name: SaveDef
entries.doc: A game's save: one record, or a fixed number of slots, each one Ruken key.

entries.name: SaveEnvelope
entries.doc: What is stored: a self-describing envelope, one Ruken key per slot.

entries.name: SaveFromNewerBuild
entries.doc: A slot was saved by a newer build. It is read-only here: nothing migrates, writes or autosaves over it.
entries.signature: class SaveFromNewerBuild extends SaveFromNewerBuildBase {}

entries.name: SaveFromNewerBuildFields
entries.doc: The fields of `SaveFromNewerBuild`.

entries.name: SaveMigration
entries.doc: One migration step of a save: version `n` data in, version `n + 1` data out (`SaveDef.migrations`).
entries.signature: type SaveMigration = (record: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown>;

entries.name: saveOf
entries.doc:
Returns the booted save when `def.key` matches.
Dies with a defect if the game booted a different save, or none: asking for a save the game never declared is
the game's mistake (as `settingsStore` does for settings).
entries.signature: function saveOf<S>(def: SaveDef<S>): Effect.Effect<Save<S>, never, Saves>;

entries.name: SaveRefused
entries.doc: A write AF refuses on its own: over a save from a newer build (M5 spec §4.3).
entries.signature: class SaveRefused extends SaveRefusedBase {}

entries.name: SaveRefusedFields
entries.doc: The fields of `SaveRefused`.

entries.name: Saves
entries.doc:
The booted game's save as a runtime service (M5 spec §4.3), as `Settings` is for settings: its key and the
`Save`, both undefined for a game without saves.

entries.name: saveService
entries.doc: Opens a game's save slots: reads the slot list from the host, then loads, writes and removes slots.
entries.signature: function saveService<S>(def: SaveDef<S>, options: SaveServiceOptions): Effect.Effect<Save<S>, HostError, Hosting | PresentationBus | Scope.Scope>;

entries.name: SaveServiceOptions
entries.doc: What the save service stamps on every write and checks on every load.

entries.name: SaveUnreadable
entries.doc:
A slot's save cannot be read: a damaged envelope, a missing or throwing migration step, or data its schema refuses
(M5 spec §6). The slot is kept untouched; only an explicit write replaces it.
entries.signature: class SaveUnreadable extends SaveUnreadableBase {}

entries.name: SaveUnreadableFields
entries.doc: The fields of `SaveUnreadable`.

entries.name: SaveWriteOptions
entries.doc: Options for `Save.write`: the slot's label on the list, and a sim snapshot to keep with the data.

entries.name: ScreenContext
entries.doc: What a screen's `enter` is given: the layer to mount into, and the screen it came from.

entries.name: ScreenDef
entries.doc:
One screen of the flow: its id, whether it pauses the sim, its kind and fonts, and `enter`, which mounts it
in its scope (closing the scope leaves the screen).

entries.name: selectPlural
entries.doc: The form for a count. A category the caller did not give falls back to `other`, which is required.

entries.name: Settings
entries.doc:
The booted game's settings as a runtime service: its key and store, both undefined for a game without
settings.

entries.name: SettingsDef
entries.doc:
A game's settings: the key it is saved under, its version, schema, defaults and migration steps, and which
fields stay on one device.

entries.name: SettingsStore
entries.doc: A game's settings value: read it, subscribe to changes, and update it (each update is saved).

entries.name: settingsStore
entries.doc:
Returns the booted settings store when def.key matches.
Dies with a defect if requested key does not match booted key (planning note 7).
entries.signature: function settingsStore<S>(def: SettingsDef<S>): Effect.Effect<SettingsStore<S>, never, Settings>;

entries.name: SlotMeta
entries.doc: A slot's header, read without migrating it.

entries.name: SlotState
entries.doc: What a slot holds, as the slot list shows it (M5 spec §4.3, §6).

entries.name: SLOW_MS
entries.doc: After this long, in ms, a download still running is reported slow (the loader says so).
entries.signature: const SLOW_MS = 8e3;

entries.name: SoundOptions
entries.doc: Options for `Audio.sound`: the bus (default `sfx`), a gain and a playback rate.

entries.name: STALL_MS
entries.doc: A download that makes no progress for this long, in ms, fails `LoadStalled`.
entries.signature: const STALL_MS = 3e4;

entries.name: STANDARD_PAD_BUTTON_MAX
entries.doc:
The highest button index of the W3C Gamepad standard mapping (0 = bottom face button … 16 = home). Only the
standard mapping is bound (DX spec §3.3); a pad without it is the device layer's to normalize.
entries.signature: const STANDARD_PAD_BUTTON_MAX = 16;

entries.name: StickDirection
entries.doc: A stick pushed past its dead zone in one direction (M4.2 reads them).
entries.signature: type StickDirection = (typeof STICK_DIRECTIONS)[number];

entries.name: SwipeIndicator
entries.doc: What a swipe indicator draws: the anchor, the thumb, and whether the thumb is steering.

entries.name: SwipeTracker
entries.doc:
Turns pointer samples into held swipes, flicks and taps for a `GestureSink` (M4 spec §4.4); it reads no
clock and touches no DOM.

entries.name: textDirection
entries.doc:
Text direction from the locale's script: the explicit script subtag, else the likely one CLDR adds
(`ar` → `Arab`). Read from `Intl.Locale#maximize`, not `getTextInfo`, which not every engine has, so
every engine gives the same answer.
entries.signature: function textDirection(locale: string): "ltr" | "rtl";

entries.name: Time
entries.doc: The time service: whether the sim is paused, and why; each reason pauses until it is resumed.

entries.name: TouchMode
entries.doc: How touch drives play: the on-screen buttons, or swipes and flicks over the whole screen (M4 spec §4.4).
entries.signature: type TouchMode = "buttons" | "swipe";

entries.name: touchModesFor
entries.doc:
The touch modes a profile offers: `buttons` when an action binds `touch`, `swipe` when one binds a swipe, flick or
tap. The camera drag works beside the buttons, so it offers no mode of its own.
entries.signature: function touchModesFor(profile: InputProfile): TouchMode[];

entries.name: TouchStickSink
entries.doc: Where the overlay's move stick goes: a vector clamped to length 1, y positive down, as a pad's axes.

entries.name: Translate
entries.doc: The typed `t` verb: `t('hello', { name })`, checked against the game's compiled messages.
entries.signature: type Translate<Messages> = <K extends keyof Messages & string>(key: K, ...inputs: InputsOf<Messages[K]>) => string;

entries.name: TURN_UNITS_PER_TURN
entries.doc: Turn units in a full turn: the heading wraps here.
entries.signature: const TURN_UNITS_PER_TURN = 65536;

entries.name: turnUnitsFromPixels
entries.doc:
`dxPx` dragged at `degPerPixel` as whole turn units: positive for a drag to the right (which way that turns the
heading is the game's convention), negated when `invert`, clamped to ±`MAX_TURN_UNITS_PER_STEP`. Halves round away
from zero, so a drag left and the same drag right are the same size. A non-finite input or a `degPerPixel` that is
not positive gives 0, and the result is never −0.
entries.signature: function turnUnitsFromPixels(dxPx: number, degPerPixel: number, invert: boolean): number;

entries.name: typedBus
entries.doc:
Cast a PresentationBus instance to a typed view with game-specific fact types.
Safe because PresentationBus stores facts dynamically by string key.
entries.signature: function typedBus<GameFacts>(bus: PresentationBus<object>): PresentationBus<GameFacts>;

entries.name: defineExtension
entries.doc: Returns its argument. It exists so the name keeps its literal type and `pnpm style` can find extensions.
entries.signature: function defineExtension<const N extends string>(def: ExtensionDef<N>): ExtensionDef<N>;

entries.name: ExtensionDef
entries.doc: One opt-in feature of a game (M1 shared contracts §2). Build it with `defineExtension`.

entries.name: ExtensionError
entries.doc: A bad extension list. Thrown, not returned, so a game's Vite build fails with `message`.

entries.name: GameConfig
entries.doc: The parts of Ruken's manifest an extension may read (`@ruken/manifest` `Manifest`, never copied).
entries.signature: type GameConfig = Pick<Manifest, "game" | "runtime" | "content">;

entries.name: ResolvedExtensions
entries.doc: Everything the runtime and the build tools need from a game's extension list, in one fixed order.

entries.name: resolveExtensions
entries.doc:
Checks the list and puts it in a fixed order. Throws `ExtensionError`, synchronously, so a game's
Vite config fails the build with the message. At run time the build has already resolved the same
list, so a throw there is a defect.
entries.signature: function resolveExtensions(defs: readonly ExtensionDef[]): ResolvedExtensions;

entries.name: RukenManifestContribution
entries.doc: What an extension may add to ruken.toml in M1: preload files. `wants` is not a manifest field (Q7).

entries.name: FakeAudioContext
entries.doc:
A recording stand-in for an `AudioContext`: what was started, stopped and automated, with a clock tests
move by hand.

entries.name: fakeAudioContext
entries.doc:
`decode` turns the bytes `decodeAudioData` receives into a buffer, or throws as the browser does for bytes that
are not audio; by default the bytes are the alias's UTF-8 text.
entries.signature: function fakeAudioContext(decode?: (bytes: ArrayBuffer) => AudioBuffer): FakeAudioContext;

entries.name: fakeBuffer
entries.doc: A decoded buffer that remembers the alias it came from, so `started` can name it.
entries.signature: const fakeBuffer: (alias: string, duration?: number) => AudioBuffer;

entries.name: fakeFetch
entries.doc: Creates an in-memory fetch implementation for deterministic loading tests.
entries.signature: function fakeFetch(routes: Readonly<Record<string, FakeRoute>>, options?: FakeFetchOptions): FakeFetchResult;

entries.name: FakeFetchOptions
entries.doc: Options for `fakeFetch`: the fetch that answers urls with no route.

entries.name: FakeFetchResult
entries.doc: The fake fetch, and the urls it was asked for and saw aborted.

entries.name: FakeGainNode
entries.doc: A gain node of `fakeAudioContext`, recording its value, its targets and its automation.

entries.name: FakeRoute
entries.doc:
How `fakeFetch` answers one url: a status, the body in chunks, a content length or type, a hang or a
network error.

entries.name: ManualFrames
entries.doc: A frame source a test drives: `advance` moves time on and runs the frame asked for, if any.

entries.name: manualFrames
entries.doc: A frame source that runs a frame only when a test advances it, starting at `startMs`.
entries.signature: function manualFrames(startMs?: number): ManualFrames;

entries.name: nullRenderer
entries.doc: A renderer that draws nothing and records each call in `log`, for runtime tests without a GPU.
entries.signature: function nullRenderer(log?: NullRendererEntry[], options?: NullRendererOptions): RendererFactory;

entries.name: NullRendererEntry
entries.doc: One call `nullRenderer` recorded.

entries.name: NullRendererOptions
entries.doc: Options for `nullRenderer`: `fail` makes it fail `RendererUnavailable`.

entries.name: RuntimeTest
entries.doc:
Test harness providing `RuntimeServices | FakeHostHandle` for screen and integration tests (spec §3.1, §8.1).
Uses `HostingTest` behind the scenes, hooks DOM layers and geometry, starts the flow if screens exist,
and yields all runtime services plus `FakeHostHandle`.
entries.signature: function RuntimeTest(options?: RuntimeTestOptions): Layer.Layer<RuntimeServices | FakeHostHandle, BootError>;

entries.name: RuntimeTestOptions
entries.doc:
What `RuntimeTest` boots: the fake host, the screens, content, settings and save, and the frames, renderer,
fetch and locale it uses.

entries.name: BoardName
entries.doc: A board a source file names, by its name and position (1-based, at the opening quote).

entries.name: boardNamesIn
entries.doc:
The boards one source file names, in source order; `undefined` when it does not parse (its typecheck already
fails, and a half-read tree could report a board that is not there). `automata check` reads files through its
own `Files` and calls this; `findUndeclaredBoards` walks the disk.
entries.signature: function boardNamesIn(file: string, code: string): BoardName[] | undefined;

entries.name: BUILD_ID_PATTERN
entries.doc:
A build's ID on the dev host: the commit's UTC time to the minute, then its short sha, for example
`202610111205-abcdef0` (FloorFifty `deploy/bin/build-tag`). Time first, so IDs sort as commits do.
The host's `deploy` script accepts only IDs matching BUILD_ID_PATTERN.
entries.signature: const BUILD_ID_PATTERN: RegExp;

entries.name: buildIdFor
entries.doc:
The build ID for a commit: its UTC time to the minute, a dash, then the first seven characters of its sha.
Throws for a `sha` that is not 7 to 40 lower-case hex digits.

entries.name: ButlerFailed
entries.doc: butler exited non-zero. Its output was already shown as it ran; the CLI exits with butler's own code.

entries.name: checkManifest
entries.doc: Checks `ruken.toml` text with Ruken's own parser, so AF accepts exactly what Ruken accepts.
entries.signature: function checkManifest(toml: string): Effect.Effect<Manifest, ManifestInvalid>;

entries.name: checkVersion
entries.doc:
A release's version must be its tag's (FloorFifty `deploy/tools/ruken-pack.ts`): the build Ruken shows as
0.10.2 is the one tagged v0.10.2. A branch build has no tag and passes. Returns what is wrong, or undefined.
entries.signature: function checkVersion(version: string, tag: string | undefined): string | undefined;

entries.name: declaredBoardsIn
entries.doc:
The board ids a `ship.config.ts` declares: the keys of its `leaderboards` object, read from the source as written
(`automata check` reads files, it does not run them). `undefined` when the file does not parse, or `leaderboards`
is not written as an object (a spread or a variable), so the check says it could not read the boards.
entries.signature: function declaredBoardsIn(code: string): string[] | undefined;

entries.name: DeclaredInputs
entries.doc: The `runtime.inputs` a `ship.config.ts` declares, with the position of its opening bracket.

entries.name: declaredInputsIn
entries.doc:
The `runtime.inputs` a `ship.config.ts` declares, read from the source as written (`automata check` reads files, it
does not run them). `undefined` when the file does not parse or `runtime.inputs` is not an array of string literals.
entries.signature: function declaredInputsIn(code: string): DeclaredInputs | undefined;

entries.name: declaredOrientationIn
entries.doc:
The `runtime.orientation` a `ship.config.ts` declares, read from the source as written (`automata check` reads
files, it does not run them). `undefined` when the file does not parse or `runtime.orientation` is not written as
a literal, so the check can say it could not read it.
entries.signature: function declaredOrientationIn(code: string): string | undefined;

entries.name: defineShipConfig
entries.doc: Identity function that gives a game's `ship.config.ts` type checking and editor completion.
entries.signature: function defineShipConfig(config: ShipConfig): ShipConfig;

entries.name: deployDev
entries.doc:
Sends a prepared build to the dev host and returns its build ID and the URL it is served at. Fails with
`ManifestInvalid` for a bad `ruken.toml` in the build, `DeployFailed` when `tar` or `ssh` exits non-zero,
or a `FileError` or `ProcessError`. The temporary staging copy is removed either way.

entries.name: DeployDevInput
entries.doc:
What `deployDev` sends and where: a prepared build folder, the commit it came from, the dev host's ssh
target and URL, and whether the build becomes the one `/` redirects to.

entries.name: DeployFailed
entries.doc: The dev host's deploy step (tar or ssh) failed; `output` is what it printed.

entries.name: EntryMissing
entries.doc: `[game] entry` names a file the build does not have.

entries.name: EnvValue
entries.doc: One variable read from a game's `.env*` files, whose value the bundle scan looks for in the build.

entries.name: FileError
entries.doc: Reading, writing, listing or removing a file failed.

entries.name: findExecutable
entries.doc: The first `name` on `pathEnv` that is an executable file, or undefined. Windows also tries .exe, .cmd, .bat.
entries.signature: function findExecutable(name: string, pathEnv?: string, platform?: NodeJS.Platform): string | undefined;

entries.name: findInputsProblems
entries.doc:
Each disagreement between `inputs` (a config's `runtime.inputs`) and what the `keys()` calls in a game's sources
bind, in `inputsProblems`' words; empty when they agree or the game has no `keys()` call to compare.
entries.signature: function findInputsProblems(gameDir: string, inputs: readonly string[]): string[];

entries.name: findOrientationMismatches
entries.doc: Every `defineGame` in a game's sources that plays in an orientation other than `declared` (its config's).
entries.signature: function findOrientationMismatches(gameDir: string, declared: string): OrientationMismatchFound[];

entries.name: findRootAbsoluteReferences
entries.doc:
Every root-absolute reference to one of the build's own files in a built folder, walking it in name order.
Reads each file's syntax (scripts, stylesheets, pages, JSON), so comments and prose are not reported.
entries.signature: function findRootAbsoluteReferences(distDir: string): RootAbsoluteReferenceFound[];

entries.name: findSecretsInBuild
entries.doc:
Every secret in a built folder. Files are read as latin1, one character per byte, so offsets are byte offsets;
each `.env` value is encoded the same way so it matches its UTF-8 bytes.
entries.signature: function findSecretsInBuild(distDir: string, envValues: readonly EnvValue[]): SecretFound[];

entries.name: findUndeclaredBoards
entries.doc: Every board a game's sources name that `declared` (its ship config's `leaderboards` keys) lacks.
entries.signature: function findUndeclaredBoards(gameDir: string, declared: readonly string[]): UndeclaredBoardFound[];

entries.name: gameOrientationsIn
entries.doc:
The orientations the `defineGame` calls in one source file play in, in source order; `undefined` when the file
does not parse (its typecheck already fails, and a half-read tree could name an orientation that is not there).
entries.signature: function gameOrientationsIn(file: string, code: string): PlayedOrientation[] | undefined;

entries.name: inputsProblems
entries.doc: Each disagreement between `runtime.inputs` and the bindings, in action order; empty when they agree.
entries.signature: function inputsProblems(inputs: readonly string[], bindings: ShipInputBindings): string[];

entries.name: isBoardSource
entries.doc: Whether `file` is one of the game's sources the board check reads (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.js`, `.mjs`).
entries.signature: const isBoardSource: (file: string) => boolean;

entries.name: isInputsSource
entries.doc: Whether `file` is one of the game's sources the check reads: not a test, whose fixture games are not shipped.
entries.signature: const isInputsSource: (file: string) => boolean;

entries.name: isOrientationSource
entries.doc: Whether `file` is one of the game's sources the check reads: not a test, whose fixture games are not shipped.
entries.signature: const isOrientationSource: (file: string) => boolean;

entries.name: ITCH_FIRST_PUSH_CHECKLIST
entries.doc:
The one-time page settings butler cannot make (PUB spec §6), printed after a channel's first push. The
"Publish to itch.io" guide (PUB.5) carries the same list.
entries.signature: const ITCH_FIRST_PUSH_CHECKLIST: string;

entries.name: ITCH_LIMITS
entries.doc: itch.io's documented limits for an HTML5 upload; "MB" is read as 10^6 bytes.

entries.name: ITCH_LIMITS_SOURCE
entries.doc: Where itch.io's limits were read, and when.

entries.name: ItchBuildInvalid
entries.doc: The build breaks one of itch.io's rules; each problem names the file and the limit.

entries.name: ItchCheck
entries.doc: The `prepare --target itch` check that failed, in the order they run (PUB spec §4).
entries.signature: type ItchCheck = "entry" | "file-count" | "path-length" | "file-size" | "case" | "ruken-toml";

entries.name: ItchConfig
entries.doc: What a game writes in `ship.config.ts`.

entries.name: itchConfigSchema
entries.doc: Checks a game's `itch` section: `project` is `user/game` in lower case, and `channel` defaults to `html5`.
entries.signature: const itchConfigSchema: z.ZodType<ItchSettings, ItchConfig>;

entries.name: ItchSettingMissing
entries.doc: `publish --target itch` lacks the config section, the key or butler; found before anything runs.
entries.signature: class ItchSettingMissing extends ItchSettingMissingBase {}

entries.name: ItchSettings
entries.doc: The checked settings, with the channel filled in.

entries.name: keysBindingsIn
entries.doc:
What the `keys()` calls in one source file bind, one `<file>:<line>:<col> keys` entry per call (and `pad` and
`gestures` entries where it binds them); empty when the file has no call; `undefined` when it does not parse (its
typecheck already fails, and a half-read tree could name a device that is not there).
entries.signature: function keysBindingsIn(file: string, code: string): ShipInputBindings | undefined;

entries.name: ManifestInputsMismatch
entries.doc: `runtime.inputs` disagrees with the game's input bindings (M4 spec §4.13, I-g).

entries.name: ManifestInvalid
entries.doc: Ruken's parser refused the generated `ruken.toml`. `problems` are Ruken's own issues, unchanged.

entries.name: OrientationMismatch
entries.doc: The game plays in an orientation its ship config's `runtime.orientation` does not send Ruken (M4.7 follow-up).

entries.name: OrientationMismatchFound
entries.doc: A game that plays in an orientation its ship config does not declare.

entries.name: parseEnvFile
entries.doc: The variables of one `.env` file: `KEY=value` lines, with `export`, quotes and `#` comments allowed.
entries.signature: function parseEnvFile(file: string, text: string): EnvValue[];

entries.name: PlayedOrientation
entries.doc: An orientation a `defineGame` call plays in, at the literal's opening quote (or at the call, when it is left out).

entries.name: portsFor
entries.doc:
The ports a checkout's test server and preview build listen on (FloorFifty `playwright.config.ts`).
Several agents run at once, each in its own worktree; with fixed ports a second run either failed on a busy
port or, reusing the first run's server, silently tested another worktree's code. So each checkout path
hashes to its own slot. AF uses 4600–4799, clear of FloorFifty's 4400–4599 on the same machine; a second
example in the same run adds a fixed offset (the ui demo +100 on the preview port, Emberwick (`games/emberwick`) +300).
CI runs one job per machine and uses the fixed pair; AF_E2E_SERVER_PORT / AF_E2E_PREVIEW_PORT override.

entries.name: prepareBuild
entries.doc:
Makes a built folder ready for `ruken publish` and the dev host (ship spec §3.3): checks the tag, the
entry page, root-absolute paths, secrets (QB-b), the leaderboards the game names (M5.7) and the orientation it plays in (M4.7) and the devices its `keys()` calls bind (M4.1), then writes `ruken.toml` once Ruken's parser accepts it. Every check
runs before the write, so a failed prepare leaves the folder as it was. Zipping and Ruken's build checks
(archive, size, file types) happen inside `ruken publish`, not here.

entries.name: PrepareInput
entries.doc:
What `prepareBuild` checks and writes into: the built folder, the ship config, and the optional release
tag, game folder and input bindings.

entries.name: prepareItch
entries.doc:
Makes a built folder ready for itch.io (PUB spec §4): the tag, root-absolute paths, secrets (QB.2: a page on
itch.io is public, so the build is scanned as Ruken's is), `index.html`, itch.io's
limits, reference case and a stray `ruken.toml` are checked in that order, and the first that fails stops
prepare before anything is written. Then `<id>-<version>-itch.zip` is written beside the build folder (not in
it, so `butler push <dist>` never uploads it), for a manual upload; butler pushes the folder itself.

The build itself must already be an itch build (`resolve.conditions: ['automata-web']`, PUB.1); that is the
game's build step, not ship's.

entries.name: PrepareItchInput
entries.doc: What `prepareItch` checks and zips: the built folder, the ship config and the release tag.

entries.name: ProcessError
entries.doc: A program could not be started (not found, not executable). A non-zero exit is not this error.

entries.name: PublishAuth
entries.doc: Exit 3: the token was missing, wrong or lacks the rights.

entries.name: PublishFailed
entries.doc: Any other exit code.

entries.name: PublishInput
entries.doc:
What `publishToRuken` needs: the prepared build folder, the game's folder, Ruken's site and token, and
whether to activate the build.

entries.name: PublishItchInput
entries.doc: What `publishToItch` needs: the built folder, the ship config, the tag, the key and where butler is.

entries.name: PublishRejected
entries.doc: Exit 1: Ruken's checks rejected the build.

entries.name: PublishTimeout
entries.doc: Exit 4: Ruken's checks took longer than the CLI waits.

entries.name: publishToItch
entries.doc:
Prepares the build for itch.io (every check of `prepareItch`), then pushes the folder with butler. It fails
before any zip or process when the `itch` section, the key or butler is missing, relays butler's exit code, and
retries nothing. `firstPush` is true when butler says the channel had no build yet.

entries.name: publishToRuken
entries.doc:
Runs Ruken's own `ruken publish` on a prepared build and returns the URL Ruken says the build is served at
(`undefined` when it prints none). Ruken's exit codes become `PublishRejected` (1), `PublishUsage` (2),
`PublishAuth` (3), `PublishTimeout` (4) and `PublishFailed` for any other.

entries.name: PublishUsage
entries.doc: Exit 2: the command line was wrong.

entries.name: readEnvValues
entries.doc: The variables of every top-level `.env*` file in the game folder; none when the folder does not exist.
entries.signature: function readEnvValues(gameDir: string): EnvValue[];

entries.name: RootAbsoluteReference
entries.doc: The build names its own files from the origin's root, which 404s under `/b/<buildId>/`.

entries.name: rukenCliPath
entries.doc:
The `ruken` bin of the vendored `@ruken/cli` package. The published `@mcthaydt/automata-ship` carries a copy of
Ruken's built CLI in `dist/vendor/ruken-cli/` (D-8, M2.4 spec §3.4); every built module sits directly in
`dist/`, so the copy is `./vendor/ruken-cli/cli.js` next to it. Running from `src` in the workspace there is
no copy, and the workspace's `@ruken/cli` dev dependency is used instead (`dist/cli.js`, next to its
`dist/index.js`). `moduleUrl` and `exists` are parameters only so tests can stand in for a built package.
entries.signature: function rukenCliPath(moduleUrl?: string, exists?: (path: string) => boolean): string;

entries.name: rukenToml
entries.doc:
The text of `ruken.toml` (Ruken manifest schema 1) for a ship config. The same config always gives the same
text.
entries.signature: function rukenToml(config: ShipConfig): string;

entries.name: scanTextForSecrets
entries.doc: Every secret in one file's text.
entries.signature: function scanTextForSecrets(file: string, text: string, envValues: readonly EnvValue[]): SecretFound[];

entries.name: SecretFound
entries.doc: A secret the bundle scan found in a built file, located without repeating the secret.

entries.name: SecretInBuild
entries.doc: The build holds a key, an `.env` value or a high-entropy string (QB-b). The message never holds the secret.

entries.name: SHIP_PACKAGE
entries.doc: The name this package is published under.
entries.signature: const SHIP_PACKAGE = "@mcthaydt/automata-ship";

entries.name: ShipConfig
entries.doc:
What a game tells ship about itself, in Ruken's own manifest shape (`@ruken/manifest`'s `Manifest`).
Keys keep Ruken's snake_case so the config reads like the `ruken.toml` it becomes. ship fills in
`schema` and `allow_eval` (always false); every other field and allowed value is Ruken's, so a field
Ruken does not define is a type error here.

entries.name: ShipInputBindings
entries.doc:
What ship reads of a game's input profile. ship is published and the profile's owner (`runtime`) is private,
so this is the read-only subset ship consumes, not a copy of the contract: a profile's `bindings` is
assignable to it.

entries.name: testRemote
entries.doc:
Pushes the current branch, dispatches CI for it, waits and returns the run's URL and one `<result>\t<job>`
line per job when it is green. Otherwise fails with a `TestRemoteFailed` whose `reason` says why (see
`TestRemoteReason`).

entries.name: TestRemoteFailed
entries.doc: `test-remote` stopped without a green run; `reason` says why and `message` says what to do.
entries.signature: class TestRemoteFailed extends TestRemoteFailedBase {}

entries.name: TestRemoteInput
entries.doc:
What `testRemote` runs and how long it waits. The timing fields are for tests: the defaults suit a real
run. `args` are the words after `test-remote`: nothing for the hosted checks, Playwright arguments for one
focused run, or `--nightly`.

entries.name: TestRemoteReason
entries.doc: Why `test-remote` stopped without a green run.
entries.signature: type TestRemoteReason = "usage" | "detached" | "uncommitted" | "push" | "dispatch" | "no-run" | "no-runner" | "timeout" | "gh-unavailable" | "red";

entries.name: UndeclaredBoard
entries.doc: The game names a leaderboard its ship config's `leaderboards` does not declare (M5 spec §4.8, L-b).

entries.name: UndeclaredBoardFound
entries.doc: A board the game's sources name that its ship config does not declare, at the call site.

entries.name: VersionMismatch
entries.doc: A release tag that is not `v<version>`.
entries.signature: class VersionMismatch extends VersionMismatchBase {}

entries.name: canonicalJson
entries.doc:
Canonical JSON: object keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace. Numbers use the ECMAScript
Number-to-string algorithm, which every engine implements identically, except that -0 is written as -0.
Throws CanonicalJsonError for anything JSON can't represent exactly: NaN, Infinity, undefined, bigint,
functions, symbols, and non-plain objects (a Date, Map, Set, typed array or class instance would otherwise
serialize as {} and hash the same as every other one; M2.1 spec §10.7).
entries.signature: function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string;

entries.name: CanonicalJsonError
entries.doc: A value canonical JSON cannot represent exactly; hashing it anyway would let different values collide.

entries.name: Command
entries.doc: Input to the sim (spec §4.4 rule 4). `source` is a player slot (u8), `seq` a per-source counter (u32).

entries.name: CommandDef
entries.doc:
A command the sim accepts as input: an id and the Zod schema its payload must match. Create one with
`defineCommand`.

entries.name: CommandRecord
entries.doc:
A command as a system reads it this tick: the player slot that sent it (`source`), its per-source `seq` and
its parsed `payload`.

entries.name: ComponentDef
entries.doc:
A component: a stable id and a flat record of typed fields. Create one with `defineComponent`; game code
addresses entity data through the definition, never through `trait`.

entries.name: createRng
entries.doc: A generator seeded from `seed` (through splitmix32): the same seed gives the same sequence in every engine.
entries.signature: function createRng(seed: number): Rng;

entries.name: createSim
entries.doc:
Creates a sim from its plugins, seed and content; async, because a plugin may create engine state (a Rapier
world). Throws for a bad `tickHz`, a duplicate definition, an unknown plugin dependency or system ordering
reference, an ordering cycle, a system name the sim reserves, or an invalid resource start. If a plugin's
engine fails to start, the engines already created are disposed first.
entries.signature: function createSim(opts: SimOptions): Promise<Sim>;

entries.name: Def
entries.doc: Anything `definePlugin`'s flat `defs` list takes (DX spec §3.2).
entries.signature: type Def = ComponentDef | CommandDef | EventDef | ResourceDef | SystemDef;

entries.name: defineCommand
entries.doc:
Defines a command by id and payload schema. Throws for an id that is not lower-case words separated by dots
or dashes.
entries.signature: function defineCommand<Z extends z.ZodType>(id: string, schema: Z): CommandDef<Z>;

entries.name: defineComponent
entries.doc:
Defines a component from an id (lower-case words separated by dots or dashes) and its fields by name and
type. `render: false` keeps it out of the renderer's deltas. Throws for a bad id, no fields, a bad field
name or an unknown field type.

entries.name: defineEvent
entries.doc:
Defines an event by id and payload schema, to emit from a system with `ctx.emit`. Events come back in
`StepResult.events`; `ctx.emit` throws for a payload that fails the schema.
entries.signature: function defineEvent<Z extends z.ZodType>(id: string, schema: Z): EventDef<Z>;

entries.name: definePlugin
entries.doc:
Defines a plugin from a name, its dependencies and its definitions, given in the keyed lists or in one flat
`defs` list sorted by kind. A plugin written either way registers the same lists and gets the same schema
hash. `config` is copied as canonical, frozen JSON, so anything that cannot hash exactly throws a
`CanonicalJsonError` here.

entries.name: defineResource
entries.doc:
Defines a resource by id, schema and starting value. `createSim` parses `init()` with the schema, so a bad
start fails there.
entries.signature: function defineResource<Z extends z.ZodType>(id: string, schema: Z, init: () => z.input<Z>): ResourceDef<Z>;

entries.name: defineSystem
entries.doc:
A system: `defineSystem(name, run)` runs in `gameplay`, `defineSystem(name, phase, run)` in that phase, and the
object form also takes `before`/`after`. All three build the same SystemDef (DX spec §3.2).

entries.name: deriveSeed
entries.doc: Seed for a named substream: FNV-1a over the name's UTF-16 code units, mixed with the root seed.
entries.signature: function deriveSeed(rootSeed: number, name: string): number;

entries.name: EntityRef
entries.doc: A live entity, addressed by its StableId. Writes are coerced per field type and mark the entity changed.

entries.name: EventDef
entries.doc: An event a system emits: an id and the Zod schema its payload must match. Create one with `defineEvent`.

entries.name: FieldRecord
entries.doc: One component's field values on an entity, by field name.
entries.signature: type FieldRecord = Record<string, number | boolean | string>;

entries.name: FieldSchema
entries.doc: A component's fields, by name.
entries.signature: type FieldSchema = Readonly<Record<string, FieldType>>;

entries.name: FieldType
entries.doc:
A component field's type: `f32`, `f64`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `entity` (a StableId, stored as a `u32`) or
`string`.
entries.signature: type FieldType = (typeof FIELD_TYPES)[number];

entries.name: FieldValue
entries.doc:
The JavaScript type a field holds: `boolean` for `bool`, `string` for `string`, `number` for every other
type.
entries.signature: type FieldValue<T extends FieldType> = T extends "bool" ? boolean : T extends "string" ? string : number;

entries.name: FieldValues
entries.doc: The writable record of values a `FieldSchema` describes.
entries.signature: type FieldValues<S extends FieldSchema> = { -readonly [K in keyof S]: FieldValue<S[K]>; };

entries.name: hex64
entries.doc: 16 lowercase hex digits.
entries.signature: function hex64(value: bigint): string;

entries.name: Phase
entries.doc: One of the six phases a tick runs through, in `PHASES` order.
entries.signature: type Phase = (typeof PHASES)[number];

entries.name: PHASES
entries.doc: Fixed phase order (spec §4.3).
entries.signature: const PHASES: readonly ["input", "prePhysics", "physics", "postPhysics", "gameplay", "cleanup"];

entries.name: PluginDef
entries.doc:
A bundle of definitions the sim registers together: components, commands, events, resources and systems,
the plugins it depends on, and optionally per-sim engine state and `config`. Create one with
`definePlugin`.

entries.name: PluginState
entries.doc:
Engine state a plugin keeps outside the ECS, such as a Rapier world (M2.1 spec §3.1). `createSim` creates
one per sim, so a PluginDef shared by many sims never shares engine state between them.

entries.name: PluginStateSetup
entries.doc: What a plugin's state may know when it is created.

entries.name: PreparedRestore
entries.doc: A plugin's parsed restore, held until the sim knows whether the whole snapshot is valid.

entries.name: RejectedCommand
entries.doc: A command `step` dropped, with the reason.

entries.name: RejectReason
entries.doc:
Why `step` dropped a command: `bad-header` (a field is missing or out of range), `unknown-command` (no
plugin defines its type), `wrong-tick` (not the sim's current tick), `duplicate-seq` (the same source and
seq twice in one step) or `invalid-payload` (it fails the command's schema).
entries.signature: type RejectReason = "bad-header" | "unknown-command" | "wrong-tick" | "duplicate-seq" | "invalid-payload";

entries.name: RenderDelta
entries.doc:
What changed for the renderer since the last delta (spec §4.7). `changed` rows carry the entity's full
render state, so a removed component shows up as its absence. `resync` deltas list every live render
entity as added; the renderer drops everything it had first.

entries.name: RenderRow
entries.doc: One entity's render-flagged components (component id -> field values).

entries.name: ResourceDef
entries.doc:
A value the sim keeps once, not on any entity: an id, a Zod schema and the `init` that gives its starting
value. Create one with `defineResource`.

entries.name: Rng
entries.doc:
A deterministic generator (xoshiro128**, 32-bit integer math only, so it is bit-exact in every engine).
Each system gets its own, seeded from the sim's seed and the system's name.

entries.name: RngState
entries.doc: The four 32-bit words of a generator's state, as `Rng.state()` copies them and snapshots store them.
entries.signature: type RngState = [number, number, number, number];

entries.name: Sim
entries.doc:
A running simulation, stepped with commands, that can snapshot, restore and hash its state. `step` is the
only way gameplay state changes. Create one with `createSim`, and `dispose` it when done.

entries.name: SIM_VERSION
entries.doc:
The sim package's version, written into replay headers for information only (M2.3 spec §3.2). A constant
rather than a build-time define, so workspace tests and un-built replays carry the real version; M2.4's
version step updates it with package.json, and version.test.ts keeps the two equal.
entries.signature: const SIM_VERSION: string;

entries.name: SimCapacityError
entries.doc: More sims are alive than Koota allows worlds (16 per process). Dispose sims you no longer need.

entries.name: SimContext
entries.doc: What a system's `run` receives each tick (spec §4.1).

entries.name: SimDisposedError
entries.doc: The sim was disposed; it holds no world any more, so every call that reads or changes state refuses.

entries.name: SimEvent
entries.doc: An event a system emitted during a step: the event's id as `type`, and its parsed `payload`.

entries.name: SimFaultedError
entries.doc:
A system threw during `step`. The tick was left half-applied, so the sim refuses `step`, `snapshot` and
`hash` until a successful `restore` (M2.1 spec §10.2). Failing closed is cheaper than rolling back every tick.

entries.name: SimOptions
entries.doc:
What `createSim` takes: the root `seed`, the `plugins`, `tickHz` (an integer from 1 to 1000, default 60)
and the `content` the systems read as `ctx.content` (default `{}`).

entries.name: SNAPSHOT_VERSION
entries.doc:
The snapshot format version this build reads and writes; a snapshot of another version fails with
`SnapshotFormatError`.
entries.signature: const SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 1;

entries.name: SnapshotFormatError
entries.doc:
Snapshot bytes that are not a valid snapshot of this format version: bad magic, an unsupported version,
truncated or malformed sections.

entries.name: SnapshotMismatchError
entries.doc:
A valid snapshot that belongs to another sim: `field` names the header value that differs (`schemaHash`,
`contentHash` or `tickHz`), with this sim's `expected` value and the snapshot's `actual` one.

entries.name: SnapshotView
entries.doc:
A readable copy of a snapshot, for diffs and reports (M2.3 spec §3.1). Plugin bytes are opaque engine state,
so they are described by length and hash only.

entries.name: sortedEntries
entries.doc: Own enumerable [key, value] pairs, sorted by key.
entries.signature: function sortedEntries<V>(obj: Readonly<Record<string, V>>): Array<[string, V]>;

entries.name: sortedKeys
entries.doc: Own enumerable string keys, sorted by UTF-16 code unit.
entries.signature: function sortedKeys(obj: object): string[];

entries.name: SpawnPart
entries.doc: A component to spawn with: the definition alone (defaults) or [definition, initial values].
entries.signature: type SpawnPart = ComponentDef | readonly [ComponentDef, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>];

entries.name: StepResult
entries.doc:
What one `step` produced: the new tick, the events emitted, the renderer's delta and the commands that were
rejected.

entries.name: SystemDef
entries.doc:
A system: a name, the phase it runs in, the systems it must run `before` or `after` within that phase, and
its `run`, called once per tick. Create one with `defineSystem`.

entries.name: SystemSpec
entries.doc: The object form of `defineSystem`: a name, a phase, the optional `before`/`after` ordering and the run.

entries.name: xxhash64
entries.doc: XXH64 of `data` with an unsigned 64-bit `seed`.
entries.signature: function xxhash64(data: Uint8Array, seed?: bigint): bigint;

entries.name: canonicalJson
entries.doc:
Canonical JSON: object keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace. Numbers use the ECMAScript
Number-to-string algorithm, which every engine implements identically, except that -0 is written as -0.
Throws CanonicalJsonError for anything JSON can't represent exactly: NaN, Infinity, undefined, bigint,
functions, symbols, and non-plain objects (a Date, Map, Set, typed array or class instance would otherwise
serialize as {} and hash the same as every other one; M2.1 spec §10.7).
entries.signature: function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string;

entries.name: hex64
entries.doc: 16 lowercase hex digits.
entries.signature: function hex64(value: bigint): string;

entries.name: utf8
entries.doc: UTF-8 encoding without TextEncoder (the sim's lib has no DOM/Web APIs). Lone surrogates become U+FFFD.
entries.signature: function utf8(s: string): Uint8Array;

entries.name: xxhash64
entries.doc: XXH64 of `data` with an unsigned 64-bit `seed`.
entries.signature: function xxhash64(data: Uint8Array, seed?: bigint): bigint;

entries.name: atan
entries.doc: Deterministic arctangent. NaN stays NaN; `-0` stays `-0`.
entries.signature: function atan(x0: number): number;

entries.name: atan2
entries.doc: Finite inputs only (sim values are finite). Signed zeros follow the built-in atan2.
entries.signature: function atan2(y: number, x: number): number;

entries.name: cos
entries.doc: Deterministic cosine, in radians. NaN for a non-finite input.
entries.signature: function cos(x: number): number;

entries.name: exp
entries.doc: Deterministic `e` to the power `x`. Infinity above about 709.78, 0 below about -745.13.
entries.signature: function exp(x: number): number;

entries.name: hypot
entries.doc: No overflow scaling: inputs must satisfy x*x + y*y < 1.7e308.
entries.signature: function hypot(x: number, y: number): number;

entries.name: log
entries.doc: Deterministic natural logarithm. NaN for a negative input, `-Infinity` for 0.
entries.signature: function log(x0: number): number;

entries.name: pow
entries.doc:
Deterministic `x` to the power `y`. An integer `y` of 64 or less in magnitude multiplies exactly; otherwise
it is `exp(y * log(x))`, and a negative `x` with a non-integer `y` is NaN.
entries.signature: function pow(x: number, y: number): number;

entries.name: sin
entries.doc: Deterministic sine, in radians. NaN for a non-finite input; `-0` stays `-0`.
entries.signature: function sin(x: number): number;

entries.name: tan
entries.doc: Deterministic tangent, in radians, as `sin(x) / cos(x)`.
entries.signature: function tan(x: number): number;

entries.name: createRecorder
entries.doc:
Starts recording `sim` from its current state, for the recorder's `step` to extend. Throws
`ReplayRecordError` for a `checkEvery` or `snapshotEvery` that is not an integer of at least 1.
entries.signature: function createRecorder(sim: Sim, options?: RecorderOptions): Recorder;

entries.name: createReplayStepper
entries.doc:
Creates a stepper over `replay`: a fresh sim built from the replay's seed and tick rate, restored from its
start snapshot. Throws `SnapshotMismatchError` when the start snapshot belongs to another schema or
content, `SnapshotFormatError` when it is malformed, and `ReplayFormatError` when the header disagrees with
the start snapshot it describes; the sim it created is disposed first.
entries.signature: function createReplayStepper(replay: Replay, setup: ReplayStepSetup): Promise<ReplayStepper>;

entries.name: decodeReplay
entries.doc:
Decodes `.replay` bytes (already inflated) into a `Replay`. Throws `ReplayFormatError`, with the byte
offset when known, for anything that is not a valid replay.
entries.signature: function decodeReplay(bytes: Uint8Array): Replay;

entries.name: DEFAULT_CHECK_EVERY
entries.doc: How often, in ticks, a recording stores a check hash when `RecorderOptions.checkEvery` is not given.
entries.signature: const DEFAULT_CHECK_EVERY = 60;

entries.name: encodeReplay
entries.doc:
Encodes a replay as `.replay` bytes before deflate. The same run encodes to the same bytes in every engine.
Throws `ReplayFormatError` for a replay that cannot be encoded.
entries.signature: function encodeReplay(replay: Replay): Uint8Array;

entries.name: packReplay
entries.doc: Encodes a replay and deflates it into `.replay` file bytes.
entries.signature: function packReplay(replay: Replay, compression: ReplayCompression): Promise<Uint8Array>;

entries.name: Recorder
entries.doc:
Steps a sim and records the run as a `Replay`. Nothing else may step the sim while it records; the recorder
refuses to continue if something did.

entries.name: RecorderOptions
entries.doc:
What a recording takes: how often to store a check hash, whether to keep a reference hash and snapshots
(goldens), and free-form `meta`.

entries.name: Replay
entries.doc:
A recorded run: its header, the start snapshot, the accepted commands by tick, check hashes along the way
and the final tick and hash. Replaying it must reproduce every hash.

entries.name: REPLAY_FORMAT
entries.doc: The `.replay` format version this build reads and writes.
entries.signature: const REPLAY_FORMAT = 1;

entries.name: REPLAY_INFLATE_MAX_BYTES
entries.doc: Larger than FloorFifty's 1 MiB because goldens carry reference snapshots; player replays may pass less.
entries.signature: const REPLAY_INFLATE_MAX_BYTES: number;

entries.name: REPLAY_MAX_TICKS
entries.doc:
The longest run a replay may hold: 2^24 ticks, over 77 hours at 60 Hz. Bounds the work a small forged file can
ask of playback (its final delta is one varint).
entries.signature: const REPLAY_MAX_TICKS: number;

entries.name: ReplayCheck
entries.doc:
A hash check at a tick: the hash the replay recorded (`expected`) and the hash the re-simulated sim has
(`actual`). A recorded command the sim now rejects reports as `expected: 'accepted'` with the rejection
reason as `actual`.

entries.name: ReplayCommand
entries.doc:
A command as a replay stores it: the sim's `Command` without its tick, which the replay's `ticks` entry
carries.

entries.name: ReplayCompression
entries.doc:
The deflate and inflate a `.replay` file needs. The sim imports no compression library, so callers pass an
adapter (testing/sim has one for Node and one for browsers).

entries.name: ReplayFormatError
entries.doc: Bytes that are not a valid `.replay` (M2.3 spec §5). `offset` is the byte where reading failed, when known.

entries.name: ReplayHeader
entries.doc:
The facts a replay needs before it plays: tick rate, seed, the schema and content hashes it was recorded
against, where it starts and how often it checks.

entries.name: ReplayRecordError
entries.doc: A recording that cannot be exact: the sim stepped outside the recorder, a payload that is not JSON, and so on.

entries.name: ReplayStepper
entries.doc:
A replay playing back one tick at a time on its own sim. Create one with `createReplayStepper`, and
`dispose` it when done.

entries.name: ReplayStepSetup
entries.doc: What a stepper needs to rebuild the recorded sim: the same `plugins` and `content` the recording sim had.

entries.name: unpackReplay
entries.doc:
Inflates `.replay` file bytes and decodes them. Throws `ReplayFormatError` for bytes that are not a
deflated replay or that inflate past `maxInflatedBytes` (default `REPLAY_INFLATE_MAX_BYTES`).

entries.name: documentScrolls
entries.doc: The document itself never scrolls; screens scroll inside declared regions.
entries.signature: function documentScrolls(doc: Document): string[];

entries.name: FakeResizeObserver
entries.doc:
Controls the fake `ResizeObserver` `installFakeResizeObserver` put in place: report a width to every
observer, then restore the original.

entries.name: fakeViewportWindow
entries.doc:
A fake window of the given size. Its `screen` defaults to that size and its `navigator` names no browser.
Resizing and the keyboard fire `resize` on the window and the visual viewport, as a browser does.

entries.name: FakeViewportWindow
entries.doc:
A stand-in for the browser window the geometry owner reads: its size, `screen`, `navigator`, visual
viewport and `resize` listeners, with methods to rotate, open the keyboard and count live listeners.

entries.name: FakeVisualViewport
entries.doc:
The visual viewport of `FakeViewportWindow`: its height (less the keyboard, if open), an offset, and
listeners for `resize`.

entries.name: findClipped
entries.doc: Each element `selector` names is tall enough for what it holds (a crushed row clips its content).
entries.signature: function findClipped(root: ParentNode, selector: string): string[];

entries.name: findCutAtSide
entries.doc:
No control is cut at a side of a declared scroll region that clips it (see `clippedBy`). A region scrolls up and
down, so a control past its side is cut where a player would not think to scroll, as a long language's options
were in a Settings list; `findOffscreenControls` passes whatever a region clips, so this is what catches a control
cut across. A region that scrolls sideways on purpose (an editor's strip of scenes) declares
`data-scroll-region="both"`: a control past its side is reached by scrolling it, and the walk out through the
regions around it stops there. A checkbox or radio is judged by its label (`pressedPart`).
entries.signature: function findCutAtSide(root: ParentNode): string[];

entries.name: findIntrusions
entries.doc:
No visible control intersects a reserved area (Ruken's strip, a keyboard), in viewport px, by its
whole box. The one exception is a control that a declared scroll region clips (see `clippedBy`)
where that region is itself clear of every area: scrolling brings it into view. An undeclared
scroller earns nothing, and a fixed control is measured where it is drawn, whatever it sits inside.
entries.signature: function findIntrusions(root: ParentNode, rects: readonly LayoutRect[]): string[];

entries.name: findOffscreenControls
entries.doc:
Every visible control is on screen, unless a declared scroll region (`[data-scroll-region]`)
clips it (see `clippedBy`): a fixed control, or one positioned outside the region, is judged
where it is drawn, since scrolling the region would never bring it into view.
entries.signature: function findOffscreenControls(root: ParentNode): string[];

entries.name: findOverlaps
entries.doc: Two elements' boxes do not overlap.
entries.signature: function findOverlaps(a: Element, b: Element): string[];

entries.name: findSmallTargets
entries.doc:
Every visible control is at least `min` square, and a primary (`data-kind="primary"`) at least
`minPrimary` tall. A checkbox or radio is pressed through its label too, so the label is its target.
entries.signature: function findSmallTargets(root: ParentNode, min: number, minPrimary: number): string[];

entries.name: findUnreachable
entries.doc:
Each element is fully inside the viewport, and the whole of it is in view: a tap at its centre
and at the middle of each edge lands on it or inside it, so nothing covers or clips any part.
entries.signature: function findUnreachable(elements: readonly Element[]): string[];

entries.name: hostDisplay
entries.doc:
Ruken's display metrics for a hosted game. Defaults are Ruken's own fixture
(`packages/protocol/src/fixtures/display.ts` at b30d31b): a 48 x 56 tab on the right, landscape.

entries.name: installFakeResizeObserver
entries.doc:
Replaces the global `ResizeObserver` with a fake that reports only the widths you give it, for components
measured under jsdom, which has no layout. Call `restore` when the test ends.
entries.signature: function installFakeResizeObserver(): FakeResizeObserver;

entries.name: LayoutRect
entries.doc:
Layout assertions as plain DOM functions (M1.6 spec §3.10), from FloorFifty's
`tests/e2e/support/layout.ts` at 122a220 (`expectReachable`, `expectControlsFit`,
`expectRowsWhole`, `expectApart`, `expectNoDocumentScroll`).

Each returns a list of human-readable problems; `[]` is a pass. They take no test framework, so
the same code runs in Vitest browser mode and inside a Playwright `page.evaluate` bundle. They
measure what a player meets: no scrolling, at the centre of what they would tap. They need a real
layout engine; in jsdom every box is 0x0.

entries.name: MountedFixture
entries.doc: A mounted Svelte fixture: the element it was mounted into and a way to unmount it.

entries.name: mountFixture
entries.doc:
Mounts a Svelte component with the given props and no renderer or host, and flushes effects so the first
render is finished. Mounts into `target`, or into a new `div` in `document.body`, which `unmount` removes.
entries.signature: function mountFixture<Props extends Record<string, unknown>>(component: Component<Props>, props: Props, target?: HTMLElement): MountedFixture;

entries.name: pressedPart
entries.doc:
What a player presses for `control`: a checkbox's or radio's label (the theme draws it as the control, and a
press anywhere on it toggles the input), else the control itself.
entries.signature: function pressedPart(control: HTMLElement): HTMLElement;

entries.name: REFERENCE_SIZES
entries.doc:
The viewports a layout is checked at: phones in both orientations, tablets, desktops, both sides of every
breakpoint and the tightest sizes, each with the classification it should get.
entries.signature: const REFERENCE_SIZES: readonly ReferenceSize[];

entries.name: ReferenceFormFactor
entries.doc: `@mcthaydt/automata-ui`'s `FormFactor`.
entries.signature: type ReferenceFormFactor = "phone-portrait" | "phone-landscape" | "tablet-portrait" | "desktop";

entries.name: ReferenceHeightTier
entries.doc: `@mcthaydt/automata-ui`'s `HeightTier`.
entries.signature: type ReferenceHeightTier = "short" | "compact" | undefined;

entries.name: ReferenceSize
entries.doc:
One viewport every primitive and screen is checked at: a name, its size, and the form factor and height
tier it must classify as.

entries.name: textSnippet
entries.doc:
A Svelte 5 snippet rendering `<tag>text</tag>`, so a test can pass `children`, `body` or an icon
to a component without writing a wrapper component (Ruken `packages/ui/src/test-snippets.ts`).
Text is escaped unless `trusted` is set, for fixture markup such as list rows.
entries.signature: function textSnippet(text: string, tag?: string, trusted?: boolean): Snippet;

entries.name: TIGHT_SIZES
entries.doc:
Sideways phones shorter than 780x270, where an open keyboard leaves the least room (framework
audit of #7, 2026-10-11). Not resting viewports a screen is laid out for: the overlays that must
keep their actions above a keyboard (ErrorPanel, the boot failure) are checked here too.
entries.signature: const TIGHT_SIZES: readonly ReferenceSize[];

entries.name: Variant
entries.doc:
A condition layered over a reference size. Each field that is set applies; the caller turns them
into the geometry owner's inputs (a covered visual viewport, Ruken's display metrics).

entries.name: VARIANTS
entries.doc:
The conditions each size is also checked under: at rest, with the on-screen keyboard open, with Ruken's
reserved strip on the right or the left, and at its TV scale.
entries.signature: const VARIANTS: readonly Variant[];

entries.name: visibleControls
entries.doc: Controls a player could see and reach: laid out, not hidden, not in an inert subtree.
entries.signature: function visibleControls(root: ParentNode): HTMLElement[];

entries.name: Direction
entries.doc: A direction on the D-pad or the stick.
entries.signature: type Direction = "up" | "down" | "left" | "right";

entries.name: Engine
entries.doc: The browser engine a matrix cell runs in.
entries.signature: type Engine = "chromium" | "webkit" | "firefox";

entries.name: FakePad
entries.doc: One standard controller in a real browser, driven through the Gamepad API the game itself reads.

entries.name: FakePadOptions
entries.doc: How the fake pad reports itself: its mapping and its id (the id picks the prompts' glyphs).

entries.name: flick
entries.doc: A quick vertical swipe of `dy` pixels within `ms` milliseconds from `from` (M4 spec I-f: 40 px in 180 ms).
entries.signature: function flick(scope: Page | Frame, from: Point, dy: number, ms: number): Promise<void>;

entries.name: hold
entries.doc: A finger down on `target`'s centre until `until` resolves true (checked once a frame), then up.
entries.signature: function hold(target: Locator, until: () => Promise<boolean>): Promise<void>;

entries.name: INPUT_MATRIX
entries.doc: M4 spec §9.1's cells, in table order: 17 cells, 22 journeys (the desktop cells run under both hosts).
entries.signature: const INPUT_MATRIX: readonly MatrixCell[];

entries.name: InputDevice
entries.doc: The device a matrix cell plays with.
entries.signature: type InputDevice = "keyboard" | "gamepad" | "touch";

entries.name: MatrixCell
entries.doc: One cell of the input × form-factor matrix: a form factor, a device and an engine, and the hosts it runs under.

entries.name: MatrixFormFactor
entries.doc: A matrix cell's form factor, each with one viewport (M4 spec §9.1).
entries.signature: type MatrixFormFactor = "phone-portrait" | "phone-landscape" | "compact" | "tablet-portrait" | "desktop";

entries.name: MatrixHost
entries.doc: Where a journey runs: under the fake Ruken host, or standalone.
entries.signature: type MatrixHost = "fake-ruken" | "standalone";

entries.name: PAD_BUTTONS
entries.doc: The standard mapping's buttons by name: south (A on an Xbox pad) is 0, Start is 9, the D-pad 12 to 15.

entries.name: PadButton
entries.doc: A standard-mapping button by name.
entries.signature: type PadButton = keyof typeof PAD_BUTTONS;

entries.name: PadMode
entries.doc: Whether a direction is held on the D-pad or the left stick.
entries.signature: type PadMode = "dpad" | "stick";

entries.name: Point
entries.doc: A point in the target frame's own CSS pixels.

entries.name: swipe
entries.doc: A finger from `from` to `to` over `ms` milliseconds, one move a frame, on whatever is under it.
entries.signature: function swipe(scope: Page | Frame, from: Point, to: Point, ms: number): Promise<void>;

entries.name: tap
entries.doc: A finger down on `target`'s centre and straight up again.
entries.signature: function tap(target: Locator): Promise<void>;

entries.name: fakeGamepads
entries.doc: `target` hears `gamepadconnected` and `gamepaddisconnected`, as `window` does in a browser.

entries.name: FakeGamepads
entries.doc: Four gamepad slots a unit test plugs pads into and presses; `getGamepads` reads them as the browser's would.

entries.name: Difference
entries.doc:
One difference between two snapshot views: its kind, where it is (`entity 4 bounce.ball.vx`), the entity's
sid when it is an entity, and both values as printed.

entries.name: diffSnapshotViews
entries.doc:
Every difference between an expected and an actual snapshot view, field by field, in a fixed order (header,
rng, resources, next id, entities, plugin bytes) so a report reads the same in every engine. Empty when
they are equal.
entries.signature: function diffSnapshotViews(expected: SnapshotView, actual: SnapshotView): Difference[];

entries.name: expectGolden
entries.doc: Throws with the formatted report unless the golden matched or was just written.
entries.signature: function expectGolden(report: GoldenReport): void;

entries.name: formatGoldenReport
entries.doc: One report as text: a line for most outcomes, and for a divergence the tick and up to 20 differences.
entries.signature: function formatGoldenReport(report: GoldenReport): string;

entries.name: GOLDEN_MAX_PACKED_BYTES
entries.doc: A golden that passes this cannot be reviewed or loaded cheaply; lower snapshotEvery's cost instead.
entries.signature: const GOLDEN_MAX_PACKED_BYTES: number;

entries.name: goldenCommands
entries.doc:
The Vitest browser commands that let golden tests read golden files in a browser: register them with
`browser: { commands: goldenCommands() }`. Only `.golden.json` and `.replay` files inside the project root
can be read, and nothing can be written.
entries.signature: function goldenCommands(options?: GoldenCommandsOptions): Record<string, BrowserCommand<[path: string], Promise<string | null>>>;

entries.name: GoldenReport
entries.doc:
What a golden check found: `pass`, `written`, `missing`, `schema-changed`, `content-changed`,
`setup-changed` or `diverged` (with the first differing tick and the fields that differ).

entries.name: nodeCompression
entries.doc: Node only. zlib is imported when first used, so importing this module in a browser costs nothing.
entries.signature: const nodeCompression: ReplayCompression;

entries.name: replayGolden
entries.doc:
Replays a golden `.replay` against the current sim and reports whether it still matches. With reference
data a divergence names the exact tick and every field that differs. With `AUTOMATA_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` in
Node and a `record` option it records the file first, then checks what it wrote. A mismatch is a report, not
a throw: pass it to `expectGolden`.
entries.signature: function replayGolden(options: ReplayGoldenOptions): Promise<GoldenReport>;

entries.name: ReplayGoldenOptions
entries.doc:
What `replayGolden` checks: the `.replay` file, the plugins and content to replay it with, and how to
record it when updating goldens.

entries.name: RoundTripFailure
entries.doc:
One case whose restored run differed from the uninterrupted one: its number, sim seed, length, restore
tick, variant and a report of what differed.

entries.name: RoundTripOptions
entries.doc:
What `snapshotRoundTripProperty` runs: the plugins, content and a command script, and how many cases of
what length to try.

entries.name: RoundTripVariant
entries.doc: How a case restores: into a `fresh` sim, or into one that has `dirty` (stepped on past the snapshot).
entries.signature: type RoundTripVariant = "fresh" | "dirty";

entries.name: simGolden
entries.doc:
Plays a scripted run and compares the sim's hash every `every` ticks with the golden JSON file, reporting
the first recorded tick that differs. With `AUTOMATA_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` in Node it records the file. Throws
for an `every` that is not an integer of 1 or more; a mismatch is a report, not a throw.
entries.signature: function simGolden(options: SimGoldenOptions): Promise<GoldenReport>;

entries.name: SimGoldenOptions
entries.doc:
What `simGolden` runs: the plugins, content, seed and scripted commands to play for `ticks` ticks, where
the golden JSON lives, and how often to record a hash.

entries.name: snapshotRoundTripProperty
entries.doc:
Checks that snapshot, restore and continue equals an uninterrupted run, over many seeds, run lengths and
restore points, alternating fresh and dirty restores. Returns `{ failures }`; an empty list means the
property held.

entries.name: streamCompression
entries.doc: Browsers and Node: CompressionStream / DecompressionStream('deflate-raw').
entries.signature: const streamCompression: ReplayCompression;

entries.doc:
The Vitest browser commands that let golden tests read golden files in a browser: register them with
`browser: { commands: goldenCommands() }`. Only `.golden.json` and `.replay` files inside the project root
can be read, and nothing can be written.
entries.signature: function goldenCommands(options?: GoldenCommandsOptions): Record<string, BrowserCommand<[path: string], Promise<string | null>>>;

entries.name: GoldenCommandsOptions
entries.doc: Options for {@link goldenCommands}.

entries.doc:
One case whose restored run differed from the uninterrupted one: its number, sim seed, length, restore
tick, variant and a report of what differed.

entries.name: RoundTripOptions

What `snapshotRoundTripProperty` runs: the plugins, content and a command script, and how many cases of
what length to try.

entries.signature: type RoundTripVariant = "fresh" | "dirty";
